title.zh: 卷三百十二 列傳第七十一 韓琦子:忠彥 曾公亮子:孝寬 孝廣 孝蘊 陳升之 吳充 王珪從父:罕 從兄:琪
title.en: Volume 312 Biographies 71: Han Qi and son: Zhongyan, Ceng Gongliang and son: Xiaokuan, Xiao Guang, Xiao Yun, Chen Shengzhi, Wu Chong, Wang Gui and uncle: Han, nephew: Qi
title.raw: 卷三百十二 列傳第七十一 韓琦子:忠彥 曾公亮子:孝寬 孝廣 孝蘊 陳升之 吳充 王珪從父:罕 從兄:琪 Volume 312 Biographies 71: Han Qi and son: Zhongyan, Ceng Gongliang and son: Xiaokuan, Xiao Guang, Xiao Yun, Chen Shengzhi, Wu Chong, Wang Gui and uncle: Han, nephew: Qi

sentences.zh: 韓琦，字稚圭，相州安陽人。

translations.literal: Han Qi, courtesy name Zhigui, was a native of Anyang in Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi, whose courtesy name was Zhigui, was a native of Anyang in Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父國華，自有傳。

translations.literal: His father Guohua has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guohua is the subject of a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 琦風骨秀異，弱冠舉進士，名在第二。

translations.literal: Qi's bearing was outstanding and unusual; in his early twenties he passed the jinshi examination, ranking second.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi had an exceptional presence and bearing. In his early twenties he passed the jinshi examination, placing second.

sentences.zh: 方唱名，太史奏日下五色雲見，左右皆賀。

translations.literal: Just as his name was being read aloud, the Grand Astrologer reported that five-colored clouds had appeared beneath the sun, and those on either side of the throne all offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Just as his name was being proclaimed, the court astrologer reported five-colored clouds appearing beneath the sun, and everyone present congratulated him.

sentences.zh: 授將作監丞、通判淄州，入直集賢院、監左藏庫。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Directorate for Palace Buildings and Prefectural Vice Commissioner of Zizhou; he entered service at the Hall of Assembled Worthies and supervised the Left Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Director of the Directorate for Palace Buildings and assigned as vice prefect of Zizhou, then entered the Hall of Assembled Worthies on special duty and supervised the Left Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 時方貴高科，多徑去為顯職，琦獨滯筦庫，眾以為非宜，琦處之自若。

translations.literal: At the time high examination graduates were greatly favored, and many took shortcuts to prominent offices; Qi alone remained stuck at the granary treasury, and the crowd thought this inappropriate, but Qi bore it with complete composure.
translations.idiomatic: At the time graduates of the highest examinations were held in high esteem, and many quickly advanced to prominent posts. Han Qi alone lingered at the state granary treasury. Many thought this unsuitable, but he remained entirely unruffled.

sentences.zh: 禁中需金帛，皆內臣直批旨取之，無印可驗，琦請復舊制，置傳宣合同司，以相防察。

translations.literal: When gold and silks were needed inside the palace, all were taken on direct edicts written by inner eunuchs, with no seal by which to verify them. Qi requested restoration of the old system and the establishment of a Transmission and Review Contract Office for mutual oversight.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the inner palace needed gold or silk, inner eunuchs would fetch it on edicts written in their own hand, with no official seal to verify them. Han Qi asked that the old system be restored and a Transmission and Review Contract Office set up so that the two sides could check each other.

sentences.zh: 又每綱運至，必俟內臣監蒞，始得受，往往數日不至，暴露廡下，衙校以為病，琦奏罷之。

translations.literal: Moreover, whenever each transport convoy arrived, receipt had to wait until an inner eunuch came to supervise; often he would not arrive for several days, and the goods were left exposed under the eaves. The clerks considered this a hardship, and Qi memorialized to abolish the practice.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, each incoming convoy had to wait for an inner eunuch to come and supervise before it could be accepted. Often he would not appear for days, leaving goods exposed under the eaves. The warehouse staff regarded this as a serious burden, and Han Qi memorialized to abolish the requirement.

sentences.zh: 歷開封府推官、三司度支判官，拜右司諫。

translations.literal: He successively served as investigating officer of the Kaifeng prefectural office and as fiscal reviewer in the Ministry of Revenue, and was appointed Remonstrator of the Right Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as investigating officer in the Kaifeng prefectural office and as fiscal reviewer in the Ministry of Revenue, then was appointed Remonstrator of the Right Bureau.

sentences.zh: 時宰相王隨、陳堯佐，參知政事韓億、石中立，在中書罕所建明，琦連疏其過，四人同日罷。

translations.literal: At the time the chief councillors Wang Sui and Chen Yaozuo, and the Vice Grand Councillors Han Yi and Shi Zhongli, rarely put forward proposals in the Secretariat. Qi submitted successive memorials detailing their faults, and all four were dismissed on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the chief councillors Wang Sui and Chen Yaozuo, together with Vice Grand Councillors Han Yi and Shi Zhongli, seldom advanced policy in the Secretariat. Han Qi submitted a series of memorials exposing their failings, and all four were dismissed on the same day.

sentences.zh: 又請停內降，抑僥倖。

translations.literal: He also requested a halt to inner-palace direct appointments and restraint on undeserved favor.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that direct appointments from within the palace be stopped and that undeserved favor be curbed.

sentences.zh: 凡事有不便，未嘗不言，每以明得失、正紀綱、親忠直、遠邪佞為急，前後七十餘疏。

translations.literal: Whenever anything was inconvenient he never failed to speak out. He always made it urgent to clarify gain and loss, rectify discipline and statutes, draw near the loyal and upright, and keep distant the wicked and fawning—more than seventy memorials in all.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever anything was amiss he spoke out without fail. He always pressed to clarify right and wrong, restore proper order, draw the loyal and upright close, and keep the wicked and fawning at a distance—more than seventy memorials in all.

sentences.zh: 王曾為相，謂之曰：「今言者不激，則多畏顧，何補上德？

translations.literal: When Wang Zeng was chief councillor, he said to him: "Nowadays remonstrators who are not forceful mostly fear and hold back—how does that aid the sovereign's virtue?
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zeng was chief councillor, he told him, "Nowadays remonstrators who are not forceful mostly hold back out of fear. How does that help the emperor's virtue?

sentences.zh: 如君言，可謂切而不迂矣。」

translations.literal: Words like yours may be called incisive without being pedantic."
translations.idiomatic: What you say may be called incisive without being pedantic."

sentences.zh: 曾聞望方崇，罕所獎與，琦聞其語，益自信。

translations.literal: Zeng's reputation was then at its height, and he rarely bestowed praise; when Qi heard these words, he became all the more confident.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zeng's reputation was then at its height, and he rarely offered praise. When Han Qi heard these words, he grew all the more confident in himself.

sentences.zh: 權知制誥。

translations.literal: He was appointed acting drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 益、利歲饑，為體量安撫使。

translations.literal: When Yi and Li circuits suffered famine that year, he was made Commissioner for Assessment and Pacification.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi and Li circuits suffered famine that year, he was appointed Commissioner for Assessment and Pacification.

sentences.zh: 異時郡縣督賦調繁急，市上供綺繡諸物不予直，琦為緩調蠲給之，逐貪殘不職吏，汰冗役數百，活饑民百九十萬。

translations.literal: In former times prefectures and counties had pressed tax levies urgently; goods such as silks and embroideries supplied to the market were not paid fair value. Qi eased levies and granted relief, drove out greedy and cruel officials who failed in duty, eliminated several hundred superfluous corvée laborers, and kept alive 1.9 million famine victims.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier years prefectures and counties had pressed tax collections harshly, and silks and embroideries supplied to the government were often not paid at fair value. Han Qi eased levies and granted relief, expelled greedy and cruel officials who neglected their duties, cut several hundred redundant corvée posts, and saved 1.9 million people from starvation.

sentences.zh: 趙元昊反，琦適自蜀歸，論西師形勢甚悉，即命為陝西安撫使。

translations.literal: When Zhao Yuanhao rebelled, Qi had just returned from Shu and discussed the situation of the western armies in great detail; he was immediately appointed Pacification Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Yuanhao rebelled, Han Qi had just returned from Shu and laid out the situation of the western armies in thorough detail. He was immediately appointed Pacification Commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 劉平與賊戰，敗，為所執，時宰入他誣，收繫平子弟，琦辨直其冤。

translations.literal: Liu Ping fought the rebels, was defeated, and was captured. The chief councillors accepted other slanders and imprisoned Ping's sons and younger brothers. Qi argued and cleared their injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ping fought the rebels, was defeated, and taken captive. The chief councillors accepted other accusations and imprisoned Ping's sons and younger brothers. Han Qi argued their case and cleared the injustice done to them.

sentences.zh: 進樞密直學士，副夏竦為經略安撫、招討使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and served as deputy to Xia Song as Commissioner for Military Affairs, Pacification, and Suppression.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and served as deputy to Xia Song as Commissioner for Military Affairs, Pacification, and Suppression.

sentences.zh: 詔遣使督出兵，琦亦欲先發以制賊，而合府固爭，元昊遂寇鎮戎。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched envoys to supervise the dispatch of troops. Qi also wished to strike first to control the rebels, but the whole headquarters stubbornly disputed this, and Yuanhao thereupon raided Zhenrong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dispatched envoys to supervise troop movements. Han Qi also wanted to strike first and seize the initiative, but the whole headquarters stubbornly opposed him, and Yuanhao then raided Zhenrong.

sentences.zh: 琦畫攻守二策馳入奏，仁宗欲用攻策，執政者難之，琦言：「元昊雖傾國入寇，眾不過四五萬人，吾逐路重兵自為守，勢分力弱，遇敵輒不支。

translations.literal: Qi drew up offensive and defensive strategies and rushed them in memorial. Emperor Renzong wished to adopt the offensive plan, but the chief administrators found it difficult. Qi said: "Although Yuanhao has thrown the whole state into invasion, his forces do not exceed forty or fifty thousand. We station heavy troops on each route merely to defend ourselves; our strength is divided and weak, and whenever we meet the enemy we cannot hold.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi drafted offensive and defensive plans and rushed them to court. Emperor Renzong wanted to adopt the offensive plan, but the chief administrators objected. Han Qi said, "Although Yuanhao has thrown his whole state into the invasion, his forces number no more than forty or fifty thousand. We station heavy troops on each route only to defend ourselves, so our strength is divided and weak and we cannot hold whenever we meet the enemy.

sentences.zh: 若倂出一道，鼓行而前，乘賊驕惰，破之必矣。」

translations.literal: If we unite on a single route and advance with drums beating, taking advantage of the rebels' arrogance and laxity, we are sure to break them."
translations.idiomatic: If we unite on a single route and advance with drums beating, taking advantage of the enemy's arrogance and laxity, we are certain to defeat them."

sentences.zh: 乃詔鄜延、涇原同出征。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued for Fuyan and Jingyuan circuits to campaign together.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued for the Fuyan and Jingyuan commands to campaign together.

sentences.zh: 既還營，元昊來求盟，琦曰：「無約而請和者，謀也。」

translations.literal: After returning to camp, Yuanhao came seeking alliance. Qi said: "One who seeks peace without a prior agreement is plotting."
translations.idiomatic: After returning to camp, Yuanhao came seeking peace. Han Qi said, "When someone seeks peace without any prior agreement, it is a ruse."

sentences.zh: 命諸將戒嚴，賊果犯山外。

translations.literal: He ordered the generals to stand on alert, and the rebels indeed attacked outside the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the generals to stand on alert, and the rebels indeed attacked beyond the mountains.

sentences.zh: 琦悉兵付大將任福，令自懷遠城趨德勝砦出賊後，如未可戰，即據險置伏，要其歸。

translations.literal: Qi entrusted all the troops to the great general Ren Fu, ordering him to set out from Huaiyuan city toward Desheng fort and strike behind the rebels; if battle were not yet feasible, he was to seize defensible ground, set ambushes, and intercept their return.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi entrusted all the troops to the great general Ren Fu, ordering him to march from Huaiyuan toward Desheng Fort and strike behind the enemy. If battle were not yet feasible, he was to seize defensible ground, set ambushes, and cut off their retreat.

sentences.zh: 及行，戒之至再。

translations.literal: When Fu set out, Qi admonished him again and again.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu set out, Han Qi warned him again and again.

sentences.zh: 又移檄申約，苟違節度，雖有功，亦斬。

translations.literal: He also sent a written order reiterating the agreement: if discipline were violated, even with merit achieved, execution would still follow.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent a written order reiterating the agreement: anyone who violated command, even if he achieved merit, would still be executed.

sentences.zh: 福竟為賊誘，沒于好水川。

translations.literal: Fu was ultimately lured by the rebels and perished at Haoshui River.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was ultimately lured into a trap by the enemy and perished at Haoshui River.

sentences.zh: 竦使人收散兵，得琦檄於福衣帶間，言罪不在琦。

translations.literal: Xia Song sent men to gather the scattered troops and found Qi's order in Fu's belt, stating that the fault did not lie with Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Song sent men to gather the scattered troops and found Han Qi's order in Fu's belt, showing that the blame did not lie with Han Qi.

sentences.zh: 琦亦上章自劾，猶奪一官，知秦州，尋復之。

translations.literal: Qi also submitted a memorial impeaching himself, yet still had one rank stripped; he was made prefect of Qinzhou and soon restored.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi also submitted a memorial impeaching himself, yet still had one rank stripped. He was made prefect of Qinzhou and soon restored.

sentences.zh: 會四路置帥，以琦兼秦鳳經略安撫、招討使。

translations.literal: When commanders were appointed for the four routes, Qi was concurrently made Commissioner for Military Affairs, Pacification, and Suppression of Qinfeng circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When commanders were appointed for the four frontier routes, Han Qi was concurrently made Commissioner for Military Affairs, Pacification, and Suppression of the Qinfeng circuit.

sentences.zh: 慶曆二年，與三帥皆換觀察使，范仲淹、龐籍、王沿不肯拜，琦獨受不辭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingli, he and the three commanders were all transferred to the post of observation commissioner. Fan Zhongyan, Pang Ji, and Wang Yan refused to accept; Qi alone accepted without demur.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qingli, he and the three commanders were all transferred to the post of observation commissioner. Fan Zhongyan, Pang Ji, and Wang Yan refused to accept, but Han Qi alone accepted without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 未幾，還舊職，為陝西四路經略安撫、招討使，屯涇州。

translations.literal: Before long he returned to his former duties as Commissioner for Military Affairs, Pacification, and Suppression of the four Shaanxi routes, stationed at Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he returned to his former duties as Commissioner for Military Affairs, Pacification, and Suppression of the four Shaanxi routes, stationed at Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 琦與范仲淹在兵間久，名重一時，人心歸之，朝廷倚以為重，故天下稱為「韓范」。

translations.literal: Qi and Fan Zhongyan had long been among the armies; their names weighed heavily in their age, people's hearts turned to them, and the court relied on them as a great weight—so the realm called them "Han and Fan."
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi and Fan Zhongyan had long served among the armies. Their names carried great weight in their time, the people's hearts turned to them, and the court relied on them heavily, so the realm called them "Han and Fan."

sentences.zh: 東兵從宿衛來，不習勞苦，琦奏增土兵以代戍，建德順軍以蔽蕭關、嗚沙之道。

translations.literal: Eastern troops coming from palace guard service were unused to hardship. Qi memorialized to increase local troops to replace garrison duty and established the Deshun Army to shield the routes of Xiaoguan and Wusha.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern troops coming from palace guard service were unused to hardship. Han Qi memorialized to increase local troops to replace garrison duty and established the Deshun Army to shield the routes through Xiaoguan and Wusha.

sentences.zh: 方謀取橫山，規河南，而元昊稱臣，召為樞密副使。

translations.literal: Just as he was planning to take Hengshan and target the region south of the river, Yuanhao submitted as a subject, and Qi was summoned as Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was planning to take Hengshan and target the region south of the river, Yuanhao submitted as a subject, and Han Qi was summoned to serve as Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 元昊介契丹為援，強邀索無厭，宰相晏殊等厭兵，將一切從之。

translations.literal: Yuanhao, with the Khitan as his backing, pressed demands without limit. Chief councillor Yan Shu and others were weary of war and were about to grant everything.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhao, backed by the Khitan, pressed his demands without limit. Chief Councillor Yan Shu and others were weary of war and were about to grant everything he asked.

sentences.zh: 琦陳其不便，條所宜先行者七事：一曰清政本，二曰念邊計，三曰擢材賢，四曰備河北，五曰固河東，六曰收民心，七曰營洛邑。

translations.literal: Qi set forth the inconveniences and listed seven matters that should be undertaken first: first, clarify the foundation of government; second, attend to frontier planning; third, promote talented worthies; fourth, prepare Hebei; fifth, secure Hedong; sixth, win the people's hearts; seventh, build the capital at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi explained why this was unwise and listed seven measures that should be undertaken first: clarify the foundations of government; attend to frontier planning; promote talented worthies; prepare Hebei; secure Hedong; win the people's hearts; and build the capital at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 繼又陳救弊八事，欲選將帥，明按察，豐財利，遏僥倖，進能吏，退不才，謹入官，去冗食。

translations.literal: He next set forth eight measures to remedy abuses: he wished to select generals and commanders, clarify inspections, enrich fiscal resources, curb undeserved favor, advance capable officials, dismiss the untalented, be strict in admissions to office, and remove redundant consumption.
translations.idiomatic: He next set forth eight measures to remedy abuses: select generals and commanders, clarify inspections, enrich fiscal resources, curb undeserved favor, advance capable officials, dismiss the untalented, be strict in admissions to office, and remove redundant posts.

sentences.zh: 謂：「數者之舉，謗必隨之，願委計輔臣，聽其注措。」

translations.literal: He said: "When such measures are undertaken, slander is sure to follow. I hope Your Majesty will entrust the planning to your assisting ministers and let them carry it out."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "When such measures are undertaken, slander is sure to follow. I hope Your Majesty will entrust the planning to your assisting ministers and let them carry it out."

sentences.zh: 帝悉嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor fully praised and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fully praised and accepted them all.

sentences.zh: 遂宣撫陝西，討平群盜張海、郭邈山；

translations.literal: He was then made Pacification Commissioner of Shaanxi and suppressed the bandit chiefs Zhang Hai and Guo Miaoshan;
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Pacification Commissioner of Shaanxi and suppressed the bandit chiefs Zhang Hai and Guo Miaoshan;

sentences.zh: 禁卒羸老不任用者，悉汰之；

translations.literal: palace guards who were weak, old, and unfit for service were all eliminated;
translations.idiomatic: palace guards who were weak, old, and unfit for service were all eliminated;

sentences.zh: 盡修鄜延城障，須敵悉歸所侵地，乃許和。

translations.literal: the fortifications of Fuyan were fully repaired; only when the enemy had wholly returned all seized territory was peace permitted.
translations.idiomatic: the fortifications of Fuyan were fully repaired; and peace was granted only after the enemy had wholly returned all seized territory.

sentences.zh: 歸陳西北四策，以為：「今當以和好為權宜，戰守為實務。

translations.literal: On his return he presented four strategies for the northwest, holding that: "At present we should take peace as an expedient measure and war and defense as the real task.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he presented four strategies for the northwest, arguing that "at present we should treat peace as an expedient measure and war and defense as the real task.

sentences.zh: 請繕甲厲兵，營修都城，密定討伐之計。」

translations.literal: I request that armor be repaired and weapons sharpened, the capital city be built up and fortified, and plans for punitive campaigns be secretly settled."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that armor be repaired and weapons sharpened, the capital be built up and fortified, and plans for punitive campaigns be settled in secret."

sentences.zh: 時二府合班奏事，琦必盡言，雖事屬中書，亦指陳其實。

translations.literal: At the time the two bureaus reported together in court audience; Qi always spoke fully, and even when a matter belonged to the Secretariat he still pointed out how things really stood.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the two bureaus reported together in court audience. Han Qi always spoke his mind fully, and even when a matter belonged to the Secretariat he still stated how things really stood.

sentences.zh: 同列或不悅，帝獨識之，曰：「韓琦性直。」

translations.literal: Some colleagues were displeased, but the emperor alone recognized him and said: "Han Qi's nature is straightforward."
translations.idiomatic: Some colleagues were displeased, but the emperor alone recognized his worth and said, "Han Qi's nature is straightforward."

sentences.zh: 琦與范仲淹、富弼皆以海內人望，同時登用，中外跂想其勳業。

translations.literal: Qi, Fan Zhongyan, and Fu Bi all enjoyed the people's esteem throughout the realm; they were promoted at the same time, and inside and outside the court all looked eagerly to their achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi, Fan Zhongyan, and Fu Bi all enjoyed the people's esteem throughout the realm. They were promoted at the same time, and inside and outside the court all looked eagerly to their achievements.

sentences.zh: 仲淹等亦以天下為己任，群小不便之，毀言日聞。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan and the others also took the realm as their own charge; petty men found this inconvenient, and slander was heard daily.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan and the others also took the realm as their own charge. Petty men found this inconvenient, and slander was heard daily.

sentences.zh: 仲淹、弼繼罷，琦為辨析，不報。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan and Fu Bi were successively dismissed; Qi argued on their behalf, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan and Fu Bi were successively dismissed. Han Qi argued on their behalf, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 尹洙與劉滬爭城水洛事，琦右洙，朝論不謂然。

translations.literal: Yin Zhu and Liu Hu disputed the matter of fortifying Shuiluo; Qi sided with Zhu, and court opinion did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhu and Liu Hu disputed the matter of fortifying Shuiluo. Han Qi sided with Zhu, and court opinion did not agree.

sentences.zh: 乃請外，以資政殿學士知揚州，徙鄆州、成德軍、定州。

translations.literal: He then requested an outside post, and as Academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance served as prefect of Yangzhou; he was transferred to Yanzhou, the Chengde army, and Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then requested an outside post and, as Academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance, served as prefect of Yangzhou. He was later transferred to Yanzhou, the Chengde army, and Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 兼安撫使，進大學士，又加觀文殿學士。

translations.literal: He concurrently served as Pacification Commissioner, was advanced to Grand Academician, and was further given the title of Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture.
translations.idiomatic: He concurrently served as Pacification Commissioner, was promoted to Grand Academician, and was further given the title of Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture.

sentences.zh: 初，定州兵狃平貝州功，需賞賚，出怨語，至欲噪城下。

translations.literal: At first the troops of Dingzhou, accustomed to the merit of pacifying Beizhou, demanded rewards and uttered resentful words, even wishing to raise an uproar beneath the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: At first the troops of Dingzhou, accustomed to the glory of pacifying Beizhou, demanded rewards and uttered resentful words, even threatening to raise an uproar beneath the city walls.

sentences.zh: 琦聞之，以為不治且亂，用軍制勒習，誅其尤無良者。

translations.literal: When Qi heard of this, he thought that if it were not corrected there would soon be disorder; he applied military regulations to enforce training and executed the worst offenders.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Qi heard of this, he thought that if the matter were not corrected there would soon be disorder. He applied military regulations to enforce training and executed the worst offenders.

sentences.zh: 士死攻戰，則賞賻其家，籍其孤嫠繼稟之，威恩並行。

translations.literal: When soldiers died in attack or battle, he rewarded and compensated their families, registered their orphans and widows, and continued their rations—awe and kindness proceeding together.
translations.idiomatic: When soldiers died in attack or battle, he rewarded and compensated their families, registered their orphans and widows, and continued their rations, combining stern authority with kindness.

sentences.zh: 又仿古三陣法，日月訓齊之，由是中山兵精勁冠河朔。

translations.literal: He also modeled the ancient three-formations method and trained them day and night to uniformity; thereby the troops of Zhongshan became the finest and strongest north of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: He also modeled the ancient three-formations method and trained them day and night until they moved as one. Thereafter the troops of Zhongshan became the finest and strongest north of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 京師發龍猛卒戍保州，在道為人害，至定，琦悉留不遣，易素教者使之北，又振活饑民數百萬。

translations.literal: The capital dispatched Dragon Fierce guards to garrison Baozhou; on the road they harmed people. When they reached Dingzhou, Qi kept them all and would not send them on, exchanged plain instructors to lead them north, and also revived several million famine victims.
translations.idiomatic: The capital dispatched Dragon Fierce guards to garrison Baozhou, and on the road they harmed people. When they reached Dingzhou, Han Qi kept them all and would not send them on, exchanged plain instructors to lead them north, and also revived several million famine victims.

sentences.zh: 璽書褒激，鄰道視以為準。

translations.literal: Imperial letters praised and encouraged him, and neighboring circuits took him as their standard.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial letters praised and encouraged him, and neighboring circuits took him as their standard.

sentences.zh: 拜武康軍節度使、知幷州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Military Commissioner of the Wukang Army and prefect of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Military Commissioner of the Wukang Army and prefect of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 承受廖浩然，怙中貴勢貪恣，既誣逐前帥李昭亮，所為益不法，琦奏還之，帝命鞭諸本省。

translations.literal: The reception officer Liao Haoran relied on the power of inner favorites and was greedy and lawless; having already slandered and driven out the former commander Li Zhaoliang, his conduct grew still more unlawful. Qi memorialized to have him recalled; the emperor ordered him flogged at the relevant ministry.
translations.idiomatic: The reception officer Liao Haoran relied on the power of inner favorites and was greedy and lawless. Having already slandered and driven out the former commander Li Zhaoliang, his conduct grew still more unlawful. Han Qi memorialized to have him recalled, and the emperor ordered him flogged at the relevant ministry.

sentences.zh: 契丹冒占天池廟地，琦召其酋豪，示以曩日彼所求修廟檄，無以對，遂歸我斥地。

translations.literal: The Khitan encroached on and seized the land of the Tianchi Temple. Qi summoned their chieftains and showed them the edict they had once requested for repairing the temple; they had no reply and therefore returned the land we had marked off.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan encroached on and seized the land of the Tianchi Temple. Han Qi summoned their chieftains and showed them the edict they had once requested for repairing the temple. They had no reply and therefore returned the land we had marked off.

sentences.zh: 既又侵耕陽武砦地，琦鑿塹立石以限之。

translations.literal: They then encroached again by plowing the land of Yangwu Stockade. Qi dug ditches and set up stones to mark the limit.
translations.idiomatic: They then encroached again by plowing the land of Yangwu Stockade. Han Qi dug ditches and set up boundary stones to mark the limit.

sentences.zh: 始，潘美鎮河東，患寇鈔，令民悉內徙，而空塞下不耕，於是忻、代、寧化、大山之北多廢壤。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Pan Mei held Hedong, he feared enemy raids and ordered the people all to move inward, leaving the area below the passes uncultivated; thus north of Xin, Dai, Ninghua, and Dashan there was much abandoned land.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning, when Pan Mei held Hedong, he feared enemy raids and ordered the people all to move inward, leaving the area below the passes uncultivated. Thus north of Xin, Dai, Ninghua, and Dashan there was much abandoned land.

sentences.zh: 琦以為此皆良田，今棄不耕，適足以資敵，將皆為所有矣。

translations.literal: Qi held that all this was fine farmland; now abandoned and uncultivated, it would only supply the enemy, and in time would all become theirs.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi held that all this was fine farmland. Now abandoned and uncultivated, it would only supply the enemy, and in time would all become theirs.

sentences.zh: 遂請距北界十里為禁地，其南則募弓箭手居之，墾田至九千六百頃。

translations.literal: He therefore requested that a zone ten li from the northern border be made forbidden ground, and south of it archer-militia be recruited to settle there; reclaimed fields reached 9,600 qing.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore requested that a zone ten li from the northern border be made forbidden ground, and south of it archer-militia be recruited to settle there. Reclaimed fields reached 9,600 qing.

sentences.zh: 久之，求知相州。

translations.literal: After a long time he requested appointment as prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he requested appointment as prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐元年，召為三司使，未至，迎拜樞密使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiayou he was summoned as Commissioner of the Ministry of Revenue; before he arrived he was met and appointed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiayou he was summoned as Commissioner of the Ministry of Revenue. Before he arrived he was met and appointed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 三年六月，拜同中書門下平章事、集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year he was appointed Grand Councillor of the Tongzhongshu Menxia type and Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year he was appointed Grand Councillor and Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 六年閏八月，遷昭文館大學士、監修國史，封儀國公。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eighth month of the sixth year he was transferred to Grand Academician of the Hall of Illustrious Literature and Supervisor of the Compilation of the National History, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eighth month of the sixth year he was transferred to Grand Academician of the Hall of Illustrious Literature and Supervisor of the Compilation of the National History, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yi.

sentences.zh: 帝既連失三王，自至和中病疾，不能御殿。

translations.literal: The emperor had already lost three princes in succession; from the Zhihe era he was ill and could not hold court in the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already lost three princes in succession. From the Zhihe era he was ill and could not hold court in the main hall.

sentences.zh: 中外惴恐，臣下爭以立嗣固根本為言，包拯、范鎮尤激切。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the court all were fearful; officials vied in speaking of establishing an heir to secure the foundation. Bao Zheng and Fan Zhen were especially forceful.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside the court all were fearful. Officials vied in urging that an heir be established to secure the foundation. Bao Zheng and Fan Zhen were especially forceful.

sentences.zh: 積五六歲，依違未之行，言者亦稍怠。

translations.literal: For five or six years accumulated, the matter wavered without being carried out, and those who spoke also gradually slackened.
translations.idiomatic: For five or six years the matter wavered without being carried out, and those who spoke out also gradually slackened.

sentences.zh: 至是，琦乘間進曰：「皇嗣者，天下安危之所系。

translations.literal: At this point Qi seized an opportunity to advance and said: "The imperial heir is what the safety and peril of the realm depend upon.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Han Qi seized an opportunity to advance and said, "The imperial heir is what the safety and peril of the realm depend upon.

sentences.zh: 自昔禍亂之起，皆由策不早定。

translations.literal: From of old the rise of calamity and disorder has all been because the plan was not settled early.
translations.idiomatic: From of old calamity and disorder have arisen because the succession was not settled early.

sentences.zh: 陛下春秋高，未有建立，何不擇宗室之賢者，以為宗廟社稷計？」

translations.literal: Your Majesty's years are advanced, yet no heir has been established—why not select a worthy member of the imperial clan for the sake of the ancestral temples and the altars of state?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's years are advanced, yet no heir has been established. Why not select a worthy member of the imperial clan for the sake of the ancestral temples and the altars of state?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「後宮將有就館者，姑待之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Someone in the rear palace is about to give birth—let us wait for that for the moment."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Someone in the rear palace is about to give birth. Let us wait for that for the moment."

sentences.zh: 已又生女。

translations.literal: Later she again bore a daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Later she again bore a daughter.

sentences.zh: 一日，琦懷《漢書·孔光傳》以進，曰：「成帝無嗣，立弟之子。

translations.literal: One day Qi brought in the biography of Kong Guang from the Book of Han and advanced, saying: "Emperor Cheng had no heir and established his younger brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: One day Han Qi brought in the biography of Kong Guang from the Book of Han and said, "Emperor Cheng had no heir and established his younger brother's son.

sentences.zh: 彼中材之主，猶能如是，況陛下乎。

translations.literal: That ruler of only middling talent could still do so—how much more Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: That ruler of only middling talent could still do so—how much more can Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 願以太祖之心為心，則無不可者。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty would take Taizu's heart as your own heart, then nothing would be impossible."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would take Taizu's heart as your own heart, then nothing would be impossible."

sentences.zh: 又與曾公亮、張昇、歐陽修極言之。

translations.literal: He also spoke to the utmost with Zeng Gongliang, Zhang Sheng, and Ouyang Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke to the utmost with Zeng Gongliang, Zhang Sheng, and Ouyang Xiu.

sentences.zh: 會司馬光、呂誨皆有請，琦進讀二疏，未及有所啟，帝遽曰：「朕有意久矣，誰可者？」

translations.literal: It happened that Sima Guang and Lü Hui both had requests. Qi advanced and read the two memorials; before he could open his mouth on anything, the emperor abruptly said: "I have had this intention for a long time—who would be suitable?"
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Sima Guang and Lü Hui both had requests. Han Qi advanced and read the two memorials. Before he could say anything further, the emperor abruptly said, "I have had this intention for a long time. Who would be suitable?"

sentences.zh: 琦皇恐對曰：「此非臣輩所可議，當出自聖擇。」

translations.literal: Qi answered in fear and trembling: "This is not something we ministers may discuss—it should come from Your Majesty's sacred choice."
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi answered in fear and trembling, "This is not something we ministers may discuss. It should come from Your Majesty's sacred choice."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「宮中嘗養二子，小者甚純，近不慧，大者可也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The palace once raised two sons. The younger is very pure-hearted but recently has not been clever; the elder will do."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The palace once raised two sons. The younger is very pure-hearted but recently has not been clever. The elder will do."

sentences.zh: 琦請其名，帝以宗實告。

translations.literal: Qi asked his name, and the emperor told him Zongshi.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi asked his name, and the emperor told him Zongshi.

sentences.zh: 宗實，英宗舊名也。

translations.literal: Zongshi was the former name of Emperor Yingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Zongshi was the former name of Emperor Yingzong.

sentences.zh: 琦等遂力贊之，議乃定。

translations.literal: Qi and the others thereupon strongly supported him, and the decision was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi and the others thereupon strongly supported him, and the decision was settled.

sentences.zh: 英宗居濮王喪，議起知宗正。

translations.literal: While Yingzong was in mourning as Prince of Pu, it was proposed to summon him to serve as Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: While Yingzong was in mourning as Prince of Pu, it was proposed to summon him to serve as Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 琦曰：「事若行，不可中止。

translations.literal: Qi said: "If this matter proceeds, it cannot be halted midway.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi said, "If this matter proceeds, it cannot be halted midway.

sentences.zh: 陛下斷自不疑，乞內中批出。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should decide without doubt and request an inner-palace draft to issue it."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should decide without doubt and request an inner-palace draft to issue it."

sentences.zh: 帝意不欲宮人知，曰：「只中書行足矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor did not wish palace women to know and said: "It is enough for the Secretariat alone to act."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not wish palace women to know and said, "It is enough for the Secretariat alone to act."

sentences.zh: 命下，英宗固辭。

translations.literal: When the order was issued, Yingzong firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: When the order was issued, Yingzong firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 帝復問琦，琦對曰：「陛下既知其賢而選之，今不敢遽當，蓋器識遠大，所以為賢也。

translations.literal: The emperor again asked Qi. Qi answered: "Your Majesty already knew his worth and chose him; now he dares not hastily accept—surely it is because his capacity and insight are far-reaching that he is worthy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again asked Han Qi. He answered, "Your Majesty already knew his worth and chose him. Now he dares not hastily accept—surely it is because his capacity and insight are far-reaching that he is worthy.

sentences.zh: 願固起之。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will firmly raise him up."
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will firmly raise him up."

sentences.zh: 英宗既終喪，猶堅臥不起。

translations.literal: After Yingzong had completed his mourning, he still lay abed firmly and would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: After Yingzong had completed his mourning, he still lay abed and firmly would not rise.

sentences.zh: 琦言：「宗正之命初出，外人皆知必為皇子，不若遂正其名。」

translations.literal: Qi said: "The order as Director of the Imperial Clan has just been issued; outsiders all know he must become the crown prince—better to regularize his title at once."
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi said, "The order appointing him Director of the Imperial Clan has just been issued. Outsiders all know he must become the crown prince. It would be better to regularize his title at once."

sentences.zh: 乃下詔立為皇子。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued establishing him as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued establishing him as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 明年，英宗嗣位，以琦為仁宗山陵使，加門下侍郎，進封衛國公。

translations.literal: The next year, when Yingzong succeeded to the throne, Qi was made Director of the Mausoleum for Renzong, promoted to Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and advanced to Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when Yingzong succeeded to the throne, Han Qi was made Director of the Mausoleum for Renzong, promoted to Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and advanced to Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 琦既輔立英宗，門人親客，或從容語及定策事，琦必正色曰：「此仁宗聖德神斷，為天下計，皇太后內助之力，臣子何與焉。」

translations.literal: Since Qi had assisted in establishing Yingzong, disciples and close guests sometimes spoke at ease of the decision-making; Qi always said sternly: "This was Renzong's sagely virtue and divine decision, planning for the realm, with the Empress Dowager's inner assistance—what have ministers to do with it?"
translations.idiomatic: Since Han Qi had assisted in establishing Yingzong, disciples and close guests sometimes spoke casually of the succession decision. He always said sternly, "This was Renzong's sagely virtue and divine decision, made for the sake of the realm, with the Empress Dowager's assistance from within the palace. What have ministers to do with it?"

sentences.zh: 英宗暴得疾，太后垂簾聽政。

translations.literal: Yingzong suddenly fell ill, and the Empress Dowager drew the curtain and held court.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong suddenly fell ill, and the Empress Dowager drew the curtain and held court.

sentences.zh: 帝疾甚，舉措或改常度，遇宦官尤少恩，左右多不悅者，乃共為讒間，兩宮遂成隙。

translations.literal: The emperor's illness was severe; his conduct sometimes departed from the usual, and he showed eunuchs especially little favor. Many of those around him were displeased and together sowed slander, so the two palaces came to a breach.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's illness was severe. His conduct sometimes departed from the usual, and he showed eunuchs especially little favor. Many of those around him were displeased and together sowed slander, so the two palaces came to a breach.

sentences.zh: 琦與歐陽修奏事簾前，太后嗚咽流涕，具道所以，琦曰：「此病固爾，病已，必不然。

translations.literal: Qi and Ouyang Xiu reported affairs before the curtain. The Empress Dowager sobbed and wept, fully explaining the reasons. Qi said: "This illness is indeed so; when the illness passes, it will surely not be so.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi and Ouyang Xiu reported affairs before the curtain. The Empress Dowager sobbed and wept, fully explaining the reasons. Han Qi said, "This illness is indeed so. When the illness passes, it will surely not be so.

sentences.zh: 子疾，母可不容之乎？」

translations.literal: When a son is ill, can a mother fail to tolerate him?"
translations.idiomatic: When a son is ill, can a mother fail to tolerate him?"

sentences.zh: 修亦委曲進言，太后意稍和，久之而罷。

translations.literal: Xiu also advanced tactful words, and the Empress Dowager's mood gradually softened; after a long while the audience ended.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu also advanced tactful words, and the Empress Dowager's mood gradually softened. After a long while the audience ended.

sentences.zh: 後數日，琦獨見上，上曰：「太后待我無恩。」

translations.literal: Several days later Qi saw the emperor alone. The emperor said: "The Empress Dowager treats me without kindness."
translations.idiomatic: Several days later Han Qi saw the emperor alone. The emperor said, "The Empress Dowager treats me without kindness."

sentences.zh: 琦對曰：「自古聖帝明王，不為少矣。

translations.literal: Qi answered: "From of old there have been no few sage emperors and enlightened kings.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi answered, "From of old there have been no few sage emperors and enlightened kings.

sentences.zh: 然獨稱舜為大孝，豈其餘盡不孝耶？

translations.literal: Yet only Shun is called greatly filial—are all the rest wholly unfilial?
translations.idiomatic: Yet only Shun is called greatly filial. Are all the rest wholly unfilial?

sentences.zh: 父母慈愛而子孝，此常事不足道；

translations.literal: When parents are loving and a son is filial, this is an ordinary matter not worth mentioning;
translations.idiomatic: When parents are loving and a son is filial, this is an ordinary matter not worth mentioning;

sentences.zh: 惟父母不慈，而子不失孝，乃為可稱。

translations.literal: only when parents are not loving yet a son does not lose filiality is it praiseworthy.
translations.idiomatic: only when parents are not loving yet a son does not lose his filiality is it praiseworthy.

sentences.zh: 但恐陛下事之未至爾，父母豈有不慈者哉。」

translations.literal: I only fear that Your Majesty's service has not yet reached the full measure—what parents are there who are not loving?"
translations.idiomatic: I only fear that Your Majesty's service has not yet reached the full measure. What parents are there who are not loving?"

sentences.zh: 帝大感悟。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly awakened.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly awakened.

sentences.zh: 及疾愈，琦請乘輿因禱雨具素服以出，人情乃安。

translations.literal: When his illness passed, Qi requested that the imperial carriage, while praying for rain, go forth in plain dress, and popular feeling was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness passed, Han Qi requested that the imperial carriage go forth in plain dress while praying for rain, and popular feeling was then settled.

sentences.zh: 太后還政，拜琦右僕射，封魏國公。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager returned power, Qi was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager returned power, Han Qi was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 夏人寇大順，琦議停歲賜，絕和市，遣使問罪。

translations.literal: The Tangut raided Dashun. Qi proposed halting the annual gifts, cutting off border markets, and dispatching envoys to demand accountability.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut raided Dashun. Han Qi proposed halting the annual gifts, cutting off border markets, and dispatching envoys to demand accountability.

sentences.zh: 樞密使文彥博難之，或舉寶元、康定事，琦曰：「諒祚，狂童也，非有元昊智計，而邊備過當時遠甚。

translations.literal: Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Wen Yanbo found it difficult. Some cited the Baoyuan and Kangding affairs. Qi said: "Liangzuo is a reckless youth; he does not have Yuanhao's cunning, and frontier preparations far exceed those of that time.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Wen Yanbo objected. Some cited the Baoyuan and Kangding affairs. Han Qi said, "Liangzuo is a reckless youth. He does not have Yuanhao's cunning, and frontier preparations far exceed those of that time.

sentences.zh: 亟詰之，必服。」

translations.literal: Press him quickly and he is sure to submit."
translations.idiomatic: Press him quickly and he is sure to submit."

sentences.zh: 既而諒祚上表謝，帝顧琦曰：「一如所料。」

translations.literal: Before long Liangzuo submitted a memorial of apology. The emperor turned to Qi and said: "Just as you foretold."
translations.idiomatic: Before long Liangzuo submitted a memorial of apology. The emperor turned to Han Qi and said, "Just as you foretold."

sentences.zh: 帝寢疾，琦入問起居，言曰：「陛下久不視朝，願早建儲，以安社稷。」

translations.literal: The emperor lay ill in bed. Qi entered to inquire after his health and said: "Your Majesty has long not held court. I hope you will early establish an heir to settle the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor lay ill in bed. Han Qi entered to inquire after his health and said, "Your Majesty has long not held court. I hope you will establish an heir early to settle the altars of state."

sentences.zh: 帝頷之，即召學士草制，立潁王。

translations.literal: The emperor nodded, immediately summoned academicians to draft the edict, and established the Prince of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded, immediately summoned academicians to draft the edict, and established the Prince of Ying.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，拜司空兼侍中，為英宗山陵使。

translations.literal: When Shenzong took the throne, Qi was appointed Minister of Works and concurrent Palace Attendant, and made Director of the Mausoleum for Yingzong.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong took the throne, Han Qi was appointed Minister of Works and concurrent Palace Attendant, and made Director of the Mausoleum for Yingzong.

sentences.zh: 琦執政三世，或病其專。

translations.literal: Qi held office through three reigns, and some faulted him for being overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi held office through three reigns, and some faulted him for being overbearing.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞王陶劾琦不赴文德殿押班為跋扈。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Tao impeached Qi for not attending the roll call at Wende Hall as overbearing conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Tao impeached Han Qi for not attending the roll call at Wende Hall, calling it overbearing conduct.

sentences.zh: 琦請去，帝為黜陶。

translations.literal: Qi requested to leave office; the emperor dismissed Tao on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi requested to leave office, and the emperor dismissed Tao on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 永厚陵復土，琦不復入中書，堅辭位。

translations.literal: When earth was returned over Yonghou Mausoleum, Qi did not re-enter the Secretariat and firmly declined his post.
translations.idiomatic: When earth was returned over Yonghou Mausoleum, Han Qi did not re-enter the Secretariat and firmly declined his post.

sentences.zh: 除鎮安武勝軍節度使、司徒兼侍中、判相州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Military Commissioner of the Zhen'an and Wusheng armies, Minister of Education and concurrent Palace Attendant, and assigned to judge Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Military Commissioner of the Zhen'an and Wusheng armies, Minister of Education and concurrent Palace Attendant, and assigned to judge Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 入對，帝泣曰：「侍中必欲去，今日已降制矣。」

translations.literal: On entering audience the emperor wept and said: "Attendant, you surely wish to leave—today the edict has already been issued."
translations.idiomatic: On entering audience the emperor wept and said, "Attendant, you surely wish to leave. Today the edict has already been issued."

sentences.zh: 賜興道坊宅一區，擢其子忠彥秘閣校理。

translations.literal: He was granted one residence in Xingdao Ward and his son Zhongyan was promoted to Collator of the Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted one residence in Xingdao Ward, and his son Zhongyan was promoted to Collator of the Imperial Library.

sentences.zh: 琦辭兩鎮，乃但領淮南。

translations.literal: Qi declined the two commands and therefore held only Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi declined the two commands and therefore held only Huainan.

sentences.zh: 會种諤擅取綏州，西邊俶擾，改判永興軍，經略陝西。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhong E seized Suizhou on his own authority; the western border was suddenly disturbed. Qi was transferred to judge the Yongxing army and made Commissioner for Military Affairs of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Zhong E seized Suizhou on his own authority, and the western border was suddenly disturbed. Han Qi was transferred to judge the Yongxing army and made Commissioner for Military Affairs of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 琦言：「邊臣肆意妄作，棄約基亂，願召二府亟決之。」

translations.literal: Qi said: "Frontier officials act recklessly on their own, abandon treaties, and lay the foundation for disorder. I hope the two bureaus may be summoned to decide this quickly."
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi said, "Frontier officials act recklessly on their own, abandon treaties, and lay the foundation for disorder. I hope the two bureaus may be summoned to decide this quickly."

sentences.zh: 琦入辭，曾公亮等方奏事，乞與琦同議。

translations.literal: When Qi entered to take leave, Zeng Gongliang and others were just reporting affairs and asked to deliberate together with Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Qi entered to take leave, Zeng Gongliang and others were just reporting affairs and asked to deliberate together with him.

sentences.zh: 帝召之，琦曰：「臣前日備員政府，所當共議。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him. Qi said: "Your servant the other day filled a post in the government and ought to have deliberated together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him. Han Qi said, "Your servant the other day filled a post in the government and ought to have deliberated together.

sentences.zh: 今日，藩臣也，不敢預聞。」

translations.literal: Today I am a frontier minister and dare not take part in hearing it."
translations.idiomatic: Today I am a frontier minister and dare not take part in hearing it."

sentences.zh: 又言：「王陶指臣為跋扈，今陛下乃舉陝西兵柄授臣，復有劾臣如陶者，則臣赤族矣。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Wang Tao charged me with overbearing conduct. Now Your Majesty is entrusting me with military authority in Shaanxi. If there is again one who impeaches me like Tao, then my whole clan will perish."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Wang Tao charged me with overbearing conduct. Now Your Majesty is entrusting me with military authority in Shaanxi. If there is again one who impeaches me like Tao, then my whole clan will perish."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「侍中猶未知朕意邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Attendant, do you still not know my intention?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Attendant, do you still not know my intention?"

sentences.zh: 琦初言綏州不當取，已而夏人誘殺楊定，琦復言：「賊既如此，綏今不可棄」。

translations.literal: Qi at first said Suizhou ought not to be taken; afterward the Tangut lured and killed Yang Ding, and Qi again said: "Since the rebels have acted thus, Suizhou cannot now be abandoned."
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi at first said Suizhou ought not to be taken. Afterward the Tangut lured and killed Yang Ding, and he again said, "Since the enemy has acted thus, Suizhou cannot now be abandoned."

sentences.zh: 樞密院以初議詰之，琦具論其故，卒存之。

translations.literal: The Bureau of Military Affairs questioned him on the initial proposal. Qi fully explained the reasons, and in the end it was kept.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Military Affairs questioned him on the initial proposal. Han Qi fully explained the reasons, and in the end Suizhou was kept.

sentences.zh: 熙寧元年七月，復請相州以歸。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Xining he again requested to return to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Xining he again requested to return to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 河北地震、河決，徒判大名府，充安撫使，得便宜從事。

translations.literal: Hebei suffered an earthquake and the Yellow River burst its banks; he was transferred to judge Daming Prefecture, made Pacification Commissioner, and granted discretionary authority.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei suffered an earthquake and the Yellow River burst its banks. He was transferred to judge Daming Prefecture, made Pacification Commissioner, and granted discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 王安石用事，出常平使者散青苗錢。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi held power and sent out Ever-Normal Granary envoys to distribute Green Sprouts money.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi held power and sent out Ever-Normal Granary envoys to distribute Green Sprouts money.

sentences.zh: 琦亟言之。

translations.literal: Qi spoke urgently against it.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi spoke urgently against it.

sentences.zh: 帝袖其疏以示宰臣，曰：「琦真忠臣，雖在外，不忘王室。

translations.literal: The emperor kept his memorial in his sleeve and showed it to the chief ministers, saying: "Qi is a true loyal minister—though outside court, he does not forget the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor kept his memorial in his sleeve and showed it to the chief ministers, saying, "Han Qi is a true loyal minister. Though outside court, he does not forget the royal house.

sentences.zh: 朕始謂可以利民，今乃害民如此。

translations.literal: I at first thought it could benefit the people; now it harms the people like this.
translations.idiomatic: I at first thought it could benefit the people. Now it harms the people like this.

sentences.zh: 且坊郭安得青苗，而亦強與之乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover, how can market wards receive Green Sprouts funds, yet they are forcibly given them?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, how can market wards receive Green Sprouts funds, yet they are forcibly given them?"

sentences.zh: 安石勃然進曰：「苟從其欲，雖坊郭何害。」

translations.literal: Anshi advanced angrily and said: "If we follow their wishes, what harm even to market wards?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi advanced angrily and said, "If we follow their wishes, what harm even to market wards?"

sentences.zh: 明日，稱疾不出。

translations.literal: The next day he claimed illness and did not appear.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he claimed illness and did not appear.

sentences.zh: 當是時，新法幾罷，安石復出，持前議益堅。

translations.literal: At that time the New Policies were nearly abolished; Anshi returned to office and held to his former views all the more firmly.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the New Policies were nearly abolished. Wang Anshi returned to office and held to his former views all the more firmly.

sentences.zh: 琦又懇奏，安石下之條例司，令其屬疏駁，刊石頒天下。

translations.literal: Qi again memorialized earnestly. Anshi sent it to the Regulations Office and ordered his subordinates to draft refutations, which were carved on stone and promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi again memorialized earnestly. Wang Anshi sent it to the Regulations Office and ordered his subordinates to draft refutations, which were carved on stone and promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 琦申辨愈切，不克從。

translations.literal: Qi's rebuttals grew still more urgent, but he could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi's rebuttals grew still more urgent, but he could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 於是請解四路安撫使，止領一路，安石欲沮琦，即從之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he requested to be relieved of the four-circuit Pacification Commissionership and hold only one circuit. Anshi wished to thwart Qi and immediately assented.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he requested to be relieved of the four-circuit Pacification Commissionership and hold only one circuit. Wang Anshi wished to thwart Han Qi and immediately assented.

sentences.zh: 六年，還判相州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he returned to judge Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he returned to judge Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹來求代北地，帝手詔訪琦，琦奏言：

translations.literal: The Khitan came seeking land north of Dai. The emperor personally drafted an edict to consult Qi, and Qi memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan came seeking land north of Dai. The emperor personally drafted an edict to consult Han Qi, and he memorialized, saying:

sentences.zh: 「臣觀近年以來，朝廷舉事，似不以大敵為恤。

translations.literal: "Your servant observes that in recent years the court's undertakings seem not to regard the great enemy with concern.
translations.idiomatic: "Your servant observes that in recent years the court's undertakings seem not to regard the great enemy with concern.

sentences.zh: 彼見形生疑，必謂我有圖復燕南意，故引先發制人之說，造為釁端。

translations.literal: Seeing our actions they grow suspicious and surely think we intend to recover the southern Yan region; therefore they invoke the doctrine of striking first to control others and manufacture provocations.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing our actions they grow suspicious and surely think we intend to recover the southern Yan region. Therefore they invoke the doctrine of striking first to control others and manufacture provocations.

sentences.zh: 所以致疑，其事有七：高麗臣屬北方，久絕朝貢，乃因商舶誘之使來，契丹知之，必謂將以圖我。

translations.literal: The matters that cause suspicion are seven in number: Koryŏ was a subject state of the north and had long ceased tribute; yet through merchant ships it was induced to come. When the Khitan learn of this, they will surely think we intend to scheme against them.
translations.idiomatic: The matters that cause suspicion are seven in number. Koryŏ was a subject state of the north and had long ceased tribute, yet through merchant ships it was induced to come. When the Khitan learn of this, they will surely think we intend to scheme against them.

sentences.zh: 一也。

translations.literal: That is the first.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first.

sentences.zh: 強取吐蕃之地以建熙河，契丹聞之，必謂行將及我。

translations.literal: Tibetan lands were forcibly taken to establish Xihe circuit; when the Khitan hear of it, they will surely think the move will soon reach them.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetan lands were forcibly taken to establish Xihe circuit. When the Khitan hear of it, they will surely think the move will soon reach them.

sentences.zh: 二也。

translations.literal: That is the second.
translations.idiomatic: That is the second.

sentences.zh: 遍植榆柳于西山，冀其成長以制蕃騎。

translations.literal: Elms and willows were planted everywhere on the western hills, hoping that when they grew they would restrain barbarian cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Elms and willows were planted everywhere on the western hills, hoping that when they grew they would restrain barbarian cavalry.

sentences.zh: 三也。

translations.literal: That is the third.
translations.idiomatic: That is the third.

sentences.zh: 創團保甲。

translations.literal: The tuanbao militia system was created.
translations.idiomatic: The tuanbao militia system was created.

sentences.zh: 四也。

translations.literal: That is the fourth.
translations.idiomatic: That is the fourth.

sentences.zh: 諸州築城鑿池。

translations.literal: Prefectures built walls and dug moats.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures built walls and dug moats.

sentences.zh: 五也。

translations.literal: That is the fifth.
translations.idiomatic: That is the fifth.

sentences.zh: 置都作院，頒弓刀新式，大作戰車。

translations.literal: A Directorate of Works was established, new models of bows and blades were issued, and war chariots were built on a large scale.
translations.idiomatic: A Directorate of Works was established, new models of bows and blades were issued, and war chariots were built on a large scale.

sentences.zh: 六也。

translations.literal: That is the sixth.
translations.idiomatic: That is the sixth.

sentences.zh: 置河北三十七將。

translations.literal: Thirty-seven commands were established in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-seven commands were established in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 七也。

translations.literal: That is the seventh.
translations.idiomatic: That is the seventh.

sentences.zh: 契丹素為敵國，因事起疑，不得不然。

translations.literal: The Khitan have long been an enemy state; because matters give rise to suspicion, it cannot be otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan have long been an enemy state. Because matters give rise to suspicion, it cannot be otherwise.

sentences.zh: 臣昔年論青苗錢事，言者輒肆厚誣，非陛下之明，幾及大戮。

translations.literal: When your servant years ago discussed Green Sprouts money, speakers freely heaped heavy slander on me; but for Your Majesty's discernment I nearly suffered capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When your servant years ago discussed Green Sprouts money, speakers freely heaped heavy slander on me. But for Your Majesty's discernment I nearly suffered capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 自此，聞新法日下，不敢復言。

translations.literal: From then on, hearing new laws issued daily, I dared not speak again.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, hearing new laws issued daily, I dared not speak again.

sentences.zh: 今親被詔問，事系安危，言及而隱，死有餘罪。

translations.literal: Now personally receiving Your Majesty's edict of inquiry, the matter concerns safety and peril; to speak and yet conceal would leave guilt even in death.
translations.idiomatic: Now personally receiving Your Majesty's edict of inquiry, the matter concerns safety and peril. To speak and yet conceal would leave guilt even in death.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗竊計，始為陛下謀者，必曰治國之本，當先聚財積穀，募兵於民，則可以鞭笞四夷。

translations.literal: Your servant has privately reckoned that those who first advised Your Majesty surely said the foundation of governing the state must first gather wealth and store grain, recruit soldiers from the people, and then one can whip the four barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has privately reckoned that those who first advised Your Majesty surely said the foundation of governing the state must first gather wealth and store grain, recruit soldiers from the people, and then one can whip the four barbarians.

sentences.zh: 故散青苗錢，使民出利；

translations.literal: Therefore Green Sprouts money was distributed so the people would pay interest;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Green Sprouts money was distributed so the people would pay interest;

sentences.zh: 為免役之法，次第取錢；

translations.literal: the exemption-from-corvée law was made and money was taken in stages;
translations.idiomatic: the exemption-from-corvée law was made and money was taken in stages;

sentences.zh: 迨置市易務，而小商細民，無所措手。

translations.literal: then the Market Exchange Office was established, and small merchants and common people had no place to set hand.
translations.idiomatic: then the Market Exchange Office was established, and small merchants and common people had nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 新制日下，更改無常，官吏茫然，不能詳記，監司督責，以刻為明。

translations.literal: New regulations issued daily, changes without constancy; officials were dazed and could not keep detailed records; supervisory commissioners pressed responsibility and took harshness as clarity.
translations.idiomatic: New regulations issued daily, with changes without constancy. Officials were dazed and could not keep detailed records. Supervisory commissioners pressed responsibility and took harshness as clarity.

sentences.zh: 今農怨於甽畝，商歎于道路，長吏不安其職，陛下不盡知也。

translations.literal: Now farmers resent in the furrows, merchants sigh on the roads, senior officials are uneasy in their posts—Your Majesty does not fully know this.
translations.idiomatic: Now farmers resent in the furrows, merchants sigh on the roads, and senior officials are uneasy in their posts. Your Majesty does not fully know this.

sentences.zh: 夫欲攘斥四夷，以興太平，而先使邦本困搖，眾心離怨，此則為陛下始謀者大誤也。

translations.literal: To wish to repel the four barbarians and raise Great Peace, yet first make the foundation of the state shaken and troubled and the people's hearts estranged and resentful—this is a great error of those who first advised Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: To wish to repel the four barbarians and raise Great Peace, yet first make the foundation of the state shaken and the people's hearts estranged and resentful—this is a great error of those who first advised Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 臣今為陛下計，謂宜遣使報聘，具言向來興作，乃修備之常，豈有他意；

translations.literal: What your servant now plans for Your Majesty is that envoys should be sent on a return visit of courtesy, fully explaining that recent undertakings are the constant practice of defense preparations—how could there be other intent;
translations.idiomatic: What your servant now plans for Your Majesty is that envoys should be sent on a return visit of courtesy, fully explaining that recent undertakings are the constant practice of defense preparations. How could there be other intent?

sentences.zh: 疆土素定，悉如舊境，不可持此造端，以隳累世之好。

translations.literal: the borders have long been fixed and all should be as in the former territory; one must not use this to create a beginning and destroy the good relations of many generations.
translations.idiomatic: The borders have long been fixed and all should be as in the former territory. One must not use this to create a beginning and destroy the good relations of many generations.

sentences.zh: 以可疑之形，如將官之類，因而罷去。

translations.literal: Where forms are suspicious, such as frontier commanders, let them therefore be abolished and removed.
translations.idiomatic: Where forms are suspicious, such as frontier commanders, let them therefore be abolished and removed.

sentences.zh: 益養民愛力，選賢任能，疏遠奸諛，進用忠鯁，使天下悅服，邊備日充。

translations.literal: Further nourish the people and cherish their strength, select the worthy and employ the able, keep distant the wicked and fawning, advance the loyal and blunt, so that the realm is pleased and submits and frontier preparations daily grow full.
translations.idiomatic: Further nourish the people and cherish their strength, select the worthy and employ the able, keep the wicked and fawning at a distance, advance the loyal and blunt, so that the realm is pleased and submits and frontier preparations daily grow stronger.

sentences.zh: 若其果自敗盟，則可一振威武，恢復故疆，攄累朝之宿憤矣。」

translations.literal: If they truly break the alliance on their own, then in one stroke martial might may be raised, former territory recovered, and the long-standing resentments of many reigns vented."
translations.idiomatic: If they truly break the alliance on their own, then in one stroke martial might may be raised, former territory recovered, and the long-standing resentments of many reigns vented."

sentences.zh: 疏上，會安石再入相，悉以所爭地與契丹，東西七百里，論者惜之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, it happened that Anshi again entered the chief councillorship and gave all the disputed land to the Khitan—seven hundred li east and west—and commentators regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, it happened that Wang Anshi again entered the chief councillorship and gave all the disputed land to the Khitan—seven hundred li east and west—and commentators regretted it.

sentences.zh: 八年，換節永興軍，再任，未拜而薨，年六十八。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he exchanged commands to the Yongxing army and took a second term, but before he could accept the appointment he died, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he exchanged commands to the Yongxing army and took a second term, but before he could accept the appointment he died, aged sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 前一夕，大星隕於治所，櫪馬皆驚。

translations.literal: On the previous night a great star fell at his administrative seat, and stable horses were all startled.
translations.idiomatic: On the previous night a great star fell at his administrative seat, and stable horses were all startled.

sentences.zh: 帝發哀苑中，哭之慟。

translations.literal: The emperor expressed mourning in the palace park and wept for him in deep grief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor expressed mourning in the palace park and wept for him in deep grief.

sentences.zh: 輟朝三日，賜銀三千兩，絹三千匹，發兩河卒為治塚，篆其碑曰「兩朝顧命定策元勳」。

translations.literal: Court was suspended for three days. He was granted three thousand taels of silver and three thousand bolts of silk; troops from the two Hebei circuits were sent to build his tomb, and his stele was inscribed: "Founding Merit of the Two Reigns in Entrusted Mandate and Settled Policy."
translations.idiomatic: Court was suspended for three days. He was granted three thousand taels of silver and three thousand bolts of silk. Troops from the two Hebei circuits were sent to build his tomb, and his stele was inscribed: "Founding Merit of the Two Reigns in Entrusted Mandate and Settled Policy."

sentences.zh: 贈尚書令，諡曰「忠獻」，配享英宗廟庭。

translations.literal: He was posthumously appointed Minister of the Imperial Secretariat; his posthumous title was "Loyal and Offering," and he was granted paired sacrifice in Yingzong's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Minister of the Imperial Secretariat. His posthumous title was "Loyal and Offering," and he was granted paired sacrifice in Yingzong's temple court.

sentences.zh: 常令其子若孫一人官於相，以護丘墓。

translations.literal: It was regularly ordered that one of his sons or grandsons hold office in Xiang to guard his tomb mound.
translations.idiomatic: It was regularly ordered that one of his sons or grandsons hold office in Xiang to guard his tomb mound.

sentences.zh: 故事，三省長官，惟尚書令為尤重，贈者必兼他官。

translations.literal: By precedent, among the chiefs of the Three Departments only the Minister of the Imperial Secretariat was especially weighty; those posthumously appointed to it must also hold another office.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, among the chiefs of the Three Departments only the Minister of the Imperial Secretariat was especially weighty. Those posthumously appointed to it must also hold another office.

sentences.zh: 至琦，乃單贈。

translations.literal: As for Qi, he alone received the single appointment.
translations.idiomatic: As for Han Qi, he alone received the single appointment.

sentences.zh: 後又詔，雖當追策，不復更加師保，蓋貴之也。

translations.literal: Later an edict also stated that though posthumous honors might be pursued, Teacher and Protector titles would not again be added—such was the honor paid him.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict also stated that though posthumous honors might be pursued, Teacher and Protector titles would not again be added—such was the honor paid him.

sentences.zh: 琦蚤有盛名，識量英偉，臨事喜慍不見於色，論者以重厚比周勃，政事比姚崇。

translations.literal: Qi early had great fame; his insight and capacity were heroic and grand. In facing affairs joy and anger did not show on his face. Commentators compared his weight and depth to Zhou Bo and his governance to Yao Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi early had great fame. His insight and capacity were heroic and grand. In facing affairs joy and anger did not show on his face. Commentators compared his weight and depth to Zhou Bo and his governance to Yao Chong.

sentences.zh: 其為學士臨邊，年甫三十，天下已稱為韓公。

translations.literal: When he was an academician on the frontier, he was barely thirty, yet the realm already called him Lord Han.
translations.idiomatic: When he was an academician on the frontier, he was barely thirty, yet the realm already called him Lord Han.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐、治平間，再決大策，以安社稷。

translations.literal: Between the Jiayou and Zhiping eras he twice settled great policies to secure the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Jiayou and Zhiping eras he twice settled great policies to secure the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 當是時，朝廷多故，琦處危疑之際，知無不為。

translations.literal: At that time the court had many troubles; Qi stood in a time of peril and doubt and did whatever he knew should be done.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court had many troubles. Han Qi stood in a time of peril and doubt and did whatever he knew should be done.

sentences.zh: 或諫曰：「公所為誠善，萬一蹉跌，豈惟身不自保，恐家無處所。」

translations.literal: Someone admonished him, saying: "What you do is truly good, but if you should stumble, not only will you fail to preserve yourself—you may fear your family will have no place to dwell."
translations.idiomatic: Someone admonished him, saying, "What you do is truly good, but if you should stumble, not only will you fail to preserve yourself. You may fear your family will have nowhere to dwell."

sentences.zh: 琦歎曰：「是何言也。

translations.literal: Qi sighed and said: "What words are these?
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi sighed and said, "What words are these?

sentences.zh: 今臣盡力事君，死生以之。

translations.literal: Now your servant serves the sovereign with all his strength, life and death following upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Now your servant serves the sovereign with all his strength, life and death following upon it.

sentences.zh: 至於成敗，天也，豈可豫憂其不濟，遂輟不為哉。」

translations.literal: As for success or failure, that is Heaven's matter—how can one beforehand worry that it will not succeed and therefore cease to act?"
translations.idiomatic: As for success or failure, that is Heaven's matter. How can one beforehand worry that it will not succeed and therefore cease to act?"

sentences.zh: 聞者愧服。

translations.literal: Those who heard were ashamed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard were ashamed and submitted.

sentences.zh: 在魏都久，遼使每過，移牒必書名，曰：「以韓公在此故也。」

translations.literal: He was long in the Wei capital; whenever Liao envoys passed through, their documents always bore his name, saying: "Because Lord Han is here."
translations.idiomatic: He was long in the Wei capital. Whenever Liao envoys passed through, their documents always bore his name, saying, "Because Lord Han is here."

sentences.zh: 忠彥使遼，遼主問知其貌類父，即命工圖之，其見重於外國也如此。

translations.literal: Zhongyan was envoy to Liao; the Liao ruler asked and learned that his appearance resembled his father's, and immediately ordered artisans to paint him—such was the esteem in which he was held by foreign states.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan was envoy to Liao. The Liao ruler asked and learned that his appearance resembled his father's, and immediately ordered artisans to paint him. Such was the esteem in which he was held by foreign states.

sentences.zh: 琦天資樸忠，折節下士，無賤貴，禮之如一。

translations.literal: Qi's natural endowment was plain and loyal; he lowered himself to honor scholars, making no distinction between low and high, treating all with the same courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi's natural endowment was plain and loyal. He lowered himself to honor scholars, making no distinction between low and high, and treated all with the same courtesy.

sentences.zh: 尤以獎拔人才為急，儻公論所與，雖意所不悅，亦收用之，故得人為多。

translations.literal: He especially made promoting talent urgent; if public opinion favored someone, even when it did not please his own mind he still employed him—therefore he gained many capable men.
translations.idiomatic: He especially made promoting talent urgent. If public opinion favored someone, even when it did not please his own mind he still employed him, and therefore he gained many capable men.

sentences.zh: 選飭群司，皆使奉法循理。

translations.literal: He selected and disciplined the various offices, all causing them to uphold the law and follow principle.
translations.idiomatic: He selected and disciplined the various offices, all causing them to uphold the law and follow principle.

sentences.zh: 其所建請，第顧義所在，無適莫心。

translations.literal: In what he proposed and requested, he looked only to where righteousness lay, with no mind of favor or disfavor.
translations.idiomatic: In what he proposed and requested, he looked only to where righteousness lay, with no mind of favor or disfavor.

sentences.zh: 在相位時，王安石有盛名，或以為可用，琦獨不然之。

translations.literal: When he was in the chief councillorship, Wang Anshi had great fame and some thought him usable; Qi alone did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: When he was chief councillor, Wang Anshi had great fame and some thought him usable. Han Qi alone did not agree.

sentences.zh: 及守相，陛辭，神宗曰：「卿去，誰可屬國者，王安石何如？」

translations.literal: When he held Xiang and took leave at the throne, Shenzong said: "When you go, who can be entrusted with the state—what of Wang Anshi?"
translations.idiomatic: When he held Xiang and took leave at the throne, Shenzong said, "When you go, who can be entrusted with the state? What of Wang Anshi?"

sentences.zh: 琦曰：「安石為翰林學士則有餘，處輔弼之地則不可。」

translations.literal: Qi said: "Anshi as Hanlin academician would be more than sufficient; to place him in an assisting and supporting post would not do."
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi said, "Wang Anshi as Hanlin academician would be more than sufficient. To place him in an assisting and supporting post would not do."

sentences.zh: 上不答。

translations.literal: The emperor did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not reply.

sentences.zh: 其鎮大名也，魏人為立生祠。

translations.literal: When he held Daming, the people of Wei built him a living shrine.
translations.idiomatic: When he held Daming, the people of Wei built him a living shrine.

sentences.zh: 相人愛之如父母，有鬥訟，傳相勸止，曰：「勿撓吾侍中也。」
