translations.idiomatic: Chong had long disliked Cai Que. Que investigated the Xiangzhou case, arresting Anchi and relatives and staff for interrogation, seeking to hook Chong's words. The emperor alone understood he had no other involvement.

sentences.zh: 及確預政，充與議變法於前，數為所詘。

translations.literal: When Que entered governance, Chong debated the reform laws before him and was repeatedly refuted.
translations.idiomatic: When Que entered governance, Chong debated the reform laws before him and was repeatedly refuted.

sentences.zh: 安南師出無功，知諫院張璪又謂充與郭逵書，止其進兵，復置獄。

translations.literal: When the Annam campaign went out without success, Remonstrance Director Zhang Can again claimed Chong had written to Guo Kui halting the advance and reopened a case.
translations.idiomatic: When the Annam campaign went out without success, Remonstrance Director Zhang Can again claimed Chong had written to Guo Kui halting the advance and reopened a case.

sentences.zh: 充既數遭同列困毀，素病瘤，積憂畏，疾益侵。

translations.literal: Having repeatedly suffered obstruction and slander from colleagues, and having long been ill with a tumor, accumulated worry and fear made his illness worsen.
translations.idiomatic: Having repeatedly suffered obstruction and slander from colleagues, and having long been ill with a tumor, accumulated worry and fear made his illness worsen.

sentences.zh: 元豐三年三月，輿歸第，罷為觀文殿大學士、西太一宮使。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Yuanfeng he was carried home in a litter, dismissed as Senior Academician of the Hall for Worthies and Commissioner of the Western Great Ultimate Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year of Yuanfeng he was carried home in a litter and dismissed as Senior Academician of the Hall for Worthies and Commissioner of the Western Great Ultimate Palace.

sentences.zh: 逾月，卒，年六十。

translations.literal: After a month he died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: After a month he died, aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 贈司空兼侍中，諡曰正憲。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works and Concurrent Palace Attendant; posthumous title Zhengxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works and Concurrent Palace Attendant, with the posthumous title Zhengxian.

sentences.zh: 充內行修飭，事兄甚謹。

translations.literal: Chong's private conduct was disciplined; he served his elder brothers with great respect.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's private conduct was disciplined, and he served his elder brothers with great respect.

sentences.zh: 為相務安靜。

translations.literal: As chief councillor he strove for quiet governance.
translations.idiomatic: As chief councillor he strove for quiet governance.

sentences.zh: 性沉密，對家人語，未嘗及國家事，所言於上，人莫知者。

translations.literal: By nature reserved and secretive, in speaking with family he never touched state affairs; what he said to the emperor no one knew.
translations.idiomatic: By nature reserved and secretive, in speaking with family he never touched state affairs. What he said to the emperor, no one knew.

sentences.zh: 將終，戒妻子勿以私事干朝廷，帝益悲之。

translations.literal: Near death he admonished wife and children not to trouble the court with private matters; the emperor grieved all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Near death he admonished wife and children not to trouble the court with private matters, and the emperor grieved all the more.

sentences.zh: 世謂充心正而力不足，譏其知不可而弗能勇退也。

translations.literal: The world said Chong's heart was upright but his strength insufficient, mocking him for knowing what was wrong yet being unable to courageously withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The world said Chong's heart was upright but his strength insufficient, mocking him for knowing what was wrong yet being unable to courageously withdraw.

sentences.zh: 子安詩、安持。

translations.literal: His sons were Anshi and Anchi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Anshi and Anchi.

sentences.zh: 安詩在元祐時為諫官、起居郎。

translations.literal: Anshi served during the Yuanyou era as remonstrator and Attendant at the Palace Archives.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi served during the Yuanyou era as remonstrator and Attendant at the Palace Archives.

sentences.zh: 安持為都水使者，遷工部侍郎，終天章閣待制。

translations.literal: Anchi was Commissioner of Waterways, promoted to Vice Minister of Works, and ended as Awaiting Edict at the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations.
translations.idiomatic: Anchi was Commissioner of Waterways, promoted to Vice Minister of Works, and ended as Awaiting Edict at the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations.

sentences.zh: 安詩子儲、安持子侔，官皆員外郎，坐與妖人張懷素通謀，誅死。

translations.literal: Anshi's son Chu and Anchi's son Mou both held the rank of Vice Director; they were executed for conspiring with the sorcerer Zhang Huaisu.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi's son Chu and Anchi's son Mou both held the rank of Vice Director. They were executed for conspiring with the sorcerer Zhang Huaisu.

sentences.zh: 王珪，字禹玉，成都華陽人，後徙舒。

translations.literal: Wang Gui, courtesy name Yuyu, was a native of Huayang in Chengdu Prefecture; later the family moved to Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui, whose courtesy name was Yuyu, was a native of Huayang in Chengdu Prefecture. Later the family moved to Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖永，事太宗為右補闕。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yong served Emperor Taizong as Remonstrator of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yong served Emperor Taizong as Remonstrator of the Right.

sentences.zh: 吳越納土，受命往均賦，至則悉除無名之算，民皆感泣。

translations.literal: When Wuyue submitted its territory, he was ordered to equalize tax assessments; on arrival he abolished all nameless levies, and the people wept with gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuyue submitted its territory, he was ordered to equalize tax assessments. On arrival he abolished all nameless levies, and the people wept with gratitude.

sentences.zh: 使還，或言其多弛賦租。

translations.literal: On returning from his mission, some said he had excessively relaxed tax and rent.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from his mission, some said he had excessively relaxed tax and rent.

sentences.zh: 帝詰之，對曰：「使新附之邦，蒙天子仁恩，臣雖得罪，死不恨。」

translations.literal: The emperor questioned him; he replied: "To let a newly submitted region receive the Son of Heaven's benevolence—even if I offend and die, I have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned him. He replied, "To let a newly submitted region receive the Son of Heaven's benevolence—even if I offend and die, I have no regret.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 珪弱歲奇警，出語驚人。

translations.literal: Gui from childhood was extraordinarily quick-witted; his words astonished people.
translations.idiomatic: Gui from childhood was extraordinarily quick-witted, and his words astonished people.

sentences.zh: 從兄琪讀其所賦，唶曰：「騏驥方生，已有千里之志，但蘭筋未就耳。」

translations.literal: His cousin Qi read what he had composed and clicked his tongue, saying: "A qiji has just been born yet already has the will to travel a thousand li—only the sinews are not yet formed."
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Qi read what he had composed and clicked his tongue, saying, "A qiji has just been born yet already has the will to travel a thousand li—only the sinews are not yet formed.

sentences.zh: 舉進士甲科，通判揚州。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the top grade and was made Vice Prefect of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the top grade and was made Vice Prefect of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 吏民皆少珪，有大校嫚不謹，捽置之法。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners all looked down on Gui for his youth; a senior military officer was disrespectful and careless, and Gui had him seized and punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners all looked down on Gui for his youth. A senior military officer was disrespectful and careless, and Gui had him seized and punished by law.

sentences.zh: 王倫犯淮南，珪議出郊掩擊之，賊遁去。

translations.literal: When Wang Lun raided Huainan, Gui proposed going outside the city to strike by surprise; the bandits fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lun raided Huainan, Gui proposed going outside the city to strike by surprise, and the bandits fled.

sentences.zh: 召直集賢院，為鹽鐵判官、修起居注。

translations.literal: Summoned to the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, he served as Salt and Iron Administrator and Compiler of the Daily Record.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, he served as Salt and Iron Administrator and Compiler of the Daily Record.

sentences.zh: 接伴契丹使，北使過魏，舊皆盛服入。

translations.literal: Escorting Khitan envoys, when northern envoys passed Wei, by custom they all entered in full dress.
translations.idiomatic: Escorting Khitan envoys, when northern envoys passed Wei, by custom they all entered in full dress.

sentences.zh: 至是，欲便服，妄云衣冠在後乘。

translations.literal: On this occasion they wished to enter in ordinary dress, falsely claiming their caps and robes were in the rear carriage.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion they wished to enter in ordinary dress, falsely claiming their caps and robes were in the rear carriage.

sentences.zh: 珪命取授之，使者愧謝。

translations.literal: Gui ordered them fetched and handed over; the envoys apologized in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Gui ordered them fetched and handed over, and the envoys apologized in shame.

sentences.zh: 遂為賀正旦使。

translations.literal: He then served as envoy to congratulate on New Year's Day.
translations.idiomatic: He then served as envoy to congratulate on New Year's Day.

sentences.zh: 進知制誥、知審官院，為翰林學士、知開封府。

translations.literal: Advanced to Drafting Director and Director of the Bureau of Personnel Review; served as Hanlin Academician and Prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Drafting Director and Director of the Bureau of Personnel Review, and served as Hanlin Academician and Prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，除喪，復為學士，兼侍讀學士。

translations.literal: When his mother died he observed mourning; when mourning ended he again became Academician and Concurrent Lecturing Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he observed mourning. When mourning ended he again became Academician and Concurrent Lecturing Academician.

sentences.zh: 先是，三聖並侑南郊，而溫成廟享獻同太室。

translations.literal: Previously the Three Sages were all enshrined at the southern suburban sacrifice, while the offerings at Empress Wencheng's temple equaled those at the Grand Chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the Three Sages were all enshrined at the southern suburban sacrifice, while the offerings at Empress Wencheng's temple equaled those at the Grand Chamber.

sentences.zh: 珪言：「三后並配，所以致孝也，而瀆乎饗帝。

translations.literal: Gui said: "Enshrining the three empresses together serves filial piety, yet it profanes the sacrifice to the Divine Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Gui said, "Enshrining the three empresses together serves filial piety, yet it profanes the sacrifice to the Divine Lord.

sentences.zh: 後宮有廟，所以廣恩也，而僭乎饗親。」

translations.literal: Having temples for the inner palace extends grace, yet it oversteps the sacrifice to kin."
translations.idiomatic: Having temples for the inner palace extends grace, yet it oversteps the sacrifice to kin.

sentences.zh: 於是專以太祖侑于郊，而改溫成廟為祠殿。

translations.literal: Thereupon only Emperor Taizu was enshrined at the suburban sacrifice, and Wencheng's temple was changed to a hall of worship.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon only Emperor Taizu was enshrined at the suburban sacrifice, and Wencheng's temple was changed to a hall of worship.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐立皇子，中書召珪作詔，珪曰：「此大事也，非面受旨不可。」

translations.literal: When the crown prince was to be established in the Jiayou era, the Secretariat summoned Gui to draft the edict. Gui said: "This is a great affair; I cannot do it without receiving the order face to face."
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was to be established in the Jiayou era, the Secretariat summoned Gui to draft the edict. Gui said, "This is a great affair. I cannot do it without receiving the order face to face.

sentences.zh: 明日請對，曰：「海內望此舉久矣，果出自聖意乎？」

translations.literal: The next day he requested an audience and said: "The realm has long looked to this act—is it truly from the sacred will?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day he requested an audience and said, "The realm has long looked to this act—is it truly from the sacred will?

sentences.zh: 仁宗曰：「朕意決矣。」

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong said: "My will is decided."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong said, "My will is decided.

sentences.zh: 珪再拜賀，始退而草詔。

translations.literal: Gui bowed twice in congratulation, then withdrew and drafted the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Gui bowed twice in congratulation, then withdrew and drafted the edict.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修聞而歎曰：「真學士也。」

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu heard and sighed: "A true Academician!"
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu heard and sighed, "A true Academician!

sentences.zh: 帝宴寶文閣，作飛白書分侍臣，命珪識歲月姓名。

translations.literal: The emperor banqueted at the Hall of Treasured Culture, wrote feibai script and distributed it among attendant ministers, and ordered Gui to inscribe the date and names.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor banqueted at the Hall of Treasured Culture, wrote feibai script and distributed it among attendant ministers, and ordered Gui to inscribe the date and names.

sentences.zh: 再宴群王，又使為序，以所御筆、墨、箋、硯賜之。

translations.literal: Banqueting the princes again, he also had Gui compose a preface and bestowed on him the brush, ink, paper, and inkstone he had personally used.
translations.idiomatic: Banqueting the princes again, he also had Gui compose a preface and bestowed on him the brush, ink, paper, and inkstone he had personally used.

sentences.zh: 英宗立，當撰先帝諡，珪言：「古者賤不誄貴，幼不誄長，故天子稱天以誄之，制諡於郊，若云受之於天者。

translations.literal: When Yingzong acceded, posthumous titles for the late emperor were to be drafted. Gui said: "In antiquity the low did not posthumously title the high, the young did not posthumously title the elder; therefore the Son of Heaven invokes Heaven to bestow the title, fashioning the posthumous name at the suburban altar, as if receiving it from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong acceded, posthumous titles for the late emperor were to be drafted. Gui said, "In antiquity the low did not posthumously title the high, the young did not posthumously title the elder. Therefore the Son of Heaven invokes Heaven to bestow the title, fashioning the posthumous name at the suburban altar, as if receiving it from Heaven.

sentences.zh: 近制，唯詞臣撰議，庶僚不得參聞，頗違稱天之義。

translations.literal: Under recent practice only drafting academicians compose the proposal and common officials may not participate—this strays from the meaning of invoking Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Under recent practice only drafting academicians compose the proposal and common officials may not participate. This strays from the meaning of invoking Heaven.

sentences.zh: 請令兩制共議。」

translations.literal: I request that both drafting divisions deliberate together."
translations.idiomatic: I request that both drafting divisions deliberate together.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: This was granted.

sentences.zh: 濮王追崇典禮，珪與侍從、禮官合議宜稱皇伯，三夫人改封大國，執政不以為然。

translations.literal: For the rituals honoring the Prince of Pu posthumously, Gui together with attendants and ritual officials jointly concluded he should be styled Imperial Uncle; the three ladies should be enfeoffed as great states—the chief administrators did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: For the rituals honoring the Prince of Pu posthumously, Gui together with attendants and ritual officials jointly concluded he should be styled Imperial Uncle and the three ladies should be enfeoffed as great states. The chief administrators did not agree.

sentences.zh: 其後三夫人之稱，卒如初議。

translations.literal: Afterward the titles of the three ladies ultimately followed the original proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the titles of the three ladies ultimately followed the original proposal.

sentences.zh: 始，珪之請對而作詔也，有密譖之者。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Gui had requested an audience to draft the edict, someone had secretly slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning, when Gui had requested an audience to draft the edict, someone had secretly slandered him.

sentences.zh: 英宗在位之四年，忽召至蘂珠殿，傳詔令兼端明殿學士，錫之盤龍金盆，諭之曰：「秘殿之職，非直器卿於翰墨間，二府員缺，即出命矣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yingzong's reign he was suddenly summoned to the Hall of Luminous Pearls. An edict was transmitted appointing him Concurrent Academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity; he was bestowed a coiling-dragon gold basin and instructed: "The secret-hall post is not merely to place your talents among brush and ink—when a vacancy opens in the Two Departments, an appointment will issue at once.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yingzong's reign he was suddenly summoned to the Hall of Luminous Pearls. An edict was transmitted appointing him Concurrent Academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity. He was bestowed a coiling-dragon gold basin and instructed, "The secret-hall post is not merely to place your talents among brush and ink. When a vacancy opens in the Two Departments, an appointment will issue at once.

sentences.zh: 曩有讒口，朕今釋然無疑。」

translations.literal: There were slanderous tongues before; I am now at ease and without doubt."
translations.idiomatic: There were slanderous tongues before. I am now at ease and without doubt.

sentences.zh: 珪謝曰：「非陛下至明，臣死無日矣。」

translations.literal: Gui thanked him, saying: "Had Your Majesty not been supremely clear, I would have had no day left to live."
translations.idiomatic: Gui thanked him, saying, "Had Your Majesty not been supremely clear, I would have had no day left to live.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，遷學士承旨。

translations.literal: When Shenzong acceded, he was transferred to Chief Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong acceded, he was transferred to Chief Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 珪典內外制十八年，最為久次，嘗因展事齋宮，賦詩有所感，帝見而憐之。

translations.literal: Gui presided over inner and outer edicts for eighteen years—the longest tenure; once during ritual observance at the purification palace he composed a poem expressing his feelings, and the emperor saw it and took pity on him.
translations.idiomatic: Gui presided over inner and outer edicts for eighteen years—the longest tenure. Once during ritual observance at the purification palace he composed a poem expressing his feelings, and the emperor saw it and took pity on him.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xining he was appointed Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xining he was appointed Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 九年，進同中書門下平章事、集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was advanced to Concurrent Grand Councillor and Senior Academician of the Hall of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was advanced to Concurrent Grand Councillor and Senior Academician of the Hall of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 元豐官制行，由禮部侍郎超授銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the Yuanfeng official system was implemented, he was promoted in one step from Vice Minister of Rites to Silver Gleam Grandee of Glory.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuanfeng official system was implemented, he was promoted in one step from Vice Minister of Rites to Silver Gleam Grandee of Glory.

sentences.zh: 五年，正三省官名，拜尚書左僕射兼門下侍郎，以蔡確為右僕射。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when the Three Department official titles were regularized, he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Concurrent Gate Head; Cai Que was made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when the Three Department official titles were regularized, he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Concurrent Gate Head, and Cai Que was made Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 先是，神宗謂執政曰：「官制將行，欲新舊人兩用之。」

translations.literal: Previously Emperor Shenzong said to the chief administrators: "When the new official system is about to be implemented, I wish to employ both new and old men.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Emperor Shenzong said to the chief administrators, "When the new official system is about to be implemented, I wish to employ both new and old men.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「御史大夫，非司馬光不可。」

translations.literal: Again he said: "For Censor-in-Chief, none but Sima Guang will do."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "For the post of Censor-in-Chief, no one but Sima Guang will do."

sentences.zh: 珪、確相顧失色。

translations.literal: Gui and Que looked at each other, their color lost.
translations.idiomatic: Gui and Zhang Dun looked at each other, their faces draining of color.

sentences.zh: 珪憂甚，不知所出。

translations.literal: Gui was deeply worried and did not know what course to take.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was deeply alarmed and could see no way out.

sentences.zh: 確曰：「陛下久欲收靈武，公能任責，則相位可保也。」

translations.literal: Que said: "Your Majesty has long wished to recover Lingzhou. If you, sir, can bear the responsibility, then the chancellorship can be preserved."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun said: "Your Majesty has long wanted to recover Lingzhou. If you, sir, will take charge of it, your place as chief minister can be kept."

sentences.zh: 珪喜，謝確。

translations.literal: Gui was pleased and thanked Que.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was delighted and thanked Zhang Dun.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗欲召司馬光，珪薦俞充帥慶，使上平西夏策。

translations.literal: The Emperor once wished to summon Sima Guang. Gui recommended Yu Chong to command Qingzhou, causing the Emperor to adopt a strategy to pacify Western Xia.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once wanted to summon Sima Guang. Wang Gui recommended Yu Chong to command Qingzhou, steering the court toward a campaign to subdue Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 珪意以為既用兵深入，必不召光，雖召，將不至。

translations.literal: Gui's idea was that once troops were sent deep in campaign, Guang would surely not be summoned; even if summoned, he would not come.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui reckoned that once the army was committed to a deep invasion, Guang would certainly not be summoned—and even if he were, he would refuse to come.

sentences.zh: 已而光果不召。

translations.literal: Before long, Guang was indeed not summoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the event, Guang was never summoned.

sentences.zh: 永樂之敗，死者十餘萬人，實珪啟之。

translations.literal: The defeat at Yongle City left more than a hundred thousand dead; in truth Gui had set it in motion.
translations.idiomatic: The disaster at Yongle City cost more than a hundred thousand lives—and Wang Gui had truly set it in motion.

sentences.zh: 八年，帝有疾，珪白皇太后，請立延安郡王為太子。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when the Emperor fell ill, Gui informed the Empress Dowager and requested that the Prince of Yan'an Commandery be established as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the emperor fell ill. Wang Gui informed the empress dowager and asked that the Prince of Yan'an Commandery be named heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 太子立，是為哲宗。

translations.literal: The heir was established; this was Emperor Zhezong.
translations.idiomatic: The heir was installed—he would reign as Emperor Zhezong.

sentences.zh: 進珪金紫光祿大夫，封岐國公。

translations.literal: Gui was promoted to Grandee of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui was promoted to Grandee of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 五月，卒於位，年六十七。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he died in office, at the age of sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he died in office, aged sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 特輟朝五日，賻金帛五千，贈太師，諡曰文恭。

translations.literal: The court specially suspended audiences for five days, granted five thousand in gold and silk as funeral gifts, posthumously honored him as Grand Preceptor, and gave the posthumous title Wen-gong.
translations.idiomatic: The court suspended audiences for five days in his honor, granted five thousand strings' worth of gold and silk as funeral gifts, posthumously ennobled him as Grand Preceptor, and gave him the posthumous title Cultured and Reverent.

sentences.zh: 賜壽昌甲第。

translations.literal: He was granted a first-rank mansion in Shouchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a first-rank mansion in the Shouchang quarter.

sentences.zh: 從父 罕

translations.literal: Paternal uncle: Han
translations.idiomatic: Paternal uncle: Wang Han

sentences.zh: 罕，字師言，以蔭知宜興縣。

translations.literal: Han, styled Shiyan, entered office through hereditary privilege as magistrate of Yixing County.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han, styled Shiyan, entered office by hereditary privilege and served as magistrate of Yixing County.

sentences.zh: 縣多湖田，歲訴水，輕重失其平。

translations.literal: The county had many lake fields; each year people petitioned about flooding, and assessments of severity lost their balance.
translations.idiomatic: The county had many lakeside fields. Every year people petitioned about flood damage, and the assessments of who should pay what were wildly uneven.

sentences.zh: 罕躬至田處，列高下為圖，明年訴牒至，按圖示之，某戶可免，某戶不可免，眾皆服。

translations.literal: Han went in person to the fields, mapped out their relative heights and lows, and the next year when petitions arrived, he showed them the map—such-and-such household could be exempted, such-and-such could not—and all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Han went to the fields himself and mapped their relative elevations. When petitions arrived the next year, he consulted the map: this household could be exempted, that one could not. Everyone accepted the ruling.

sentences.zh: 范仲淹在潤，奏下其式于諸道。

translations.literal: When Fan Zhongyan was in Runzhou, he memorialized the throne to promulgate Han's method to all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Zhongyan was serving in Runzhou, he memorialized the throne to spread Han's method across every circuit.

sentences.zh: 西方用兵，仍年科箭羽于東南，價踴貴，富室至豫貯以待鬻。

translations.literal: When war was waged in the west, arrow feathers were levied year after year from the southeast, prices leaped high, and wealthy households even stored them in advance to sell.
translations.idiomatic: With war raging in the west, the court levied arrow feathers on the southeast year after year. Prices soared, and wealthy households even stockpiled feathers in advance to sell at a profit.

sentences.zh: 罕白郡守，倍其直市之，而令民輸錢。

translations.literal: Han told the prefect to pay double the market price to buy them up and have the people pay in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Han advised the prefect to buy up the feathers at double the market price and have the people pay their quota in cash instead.

sentences.zh: 旁州聞之，皆願如常州法。

translations.literal: Neighboring prefectures heard of this and all wished to follow Changzhou's method.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring prefectures heard of the scheme and all wanted to adopt Changzhou's approach.

sentences.zh: 累遷戶部判官。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Assistant Section Chief in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Assistant Section Chief in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 修太宗別廟，中貴人大慮材，將一新之。

translations.literal: When renovating Emperor Taizong's separate temple, a senior eunuch greatly overestimated the timber needed and intended to rebuild it entirely anew.
translations.idiomatic: During repairs to Emperor Taizong's separate temple, a senior eunuch vastly overestimated the timber required and planned to rebuild the whole structure from scratch.

sentences.zh: 罕白是特歲久丹漆黯暗，但當致飾耳，榱櫨皆如故，唯易一楹，省緡錢十萬。

translations.literal: Han reported that this was merely because years had darkened the cinnabar lacquer and it needed only refurbishment; the rafters and beams could all remain as they were, only one pillar needed replacing, saving a hundred thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Han reported that the lacquer had merely darkened with age and needed only refurbishing. The rafters and beams could all stay in place; only one pillar needed replacing—a saving of a hundred thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 出為廣東轉運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred out to serve as Transport Commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted out as Transport Commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 儂智高入寇，罕行部在潮，廣州守仲簡自圍中遣書邀罕，罕報曰：「吾家亦受困，非不欲歸，顧獨歸無益，當求所以相濟者。」

translations.literal: When Nong Zhigao invaded, Han was on circuit inspection in Chaozhou. Zhong Jian, prefect of Guangzhou, sent a letter from within the siege inviting Han. Han replied: "My own household is also besieged—it is not that I do not wish to return, but returning alone would do no good. One must find a way to help each other."
translations.idiomatic: When Nong Zhigao invaded, Han was making a circuit inspection in Chaozhou. Zhong Jian, the besieged prefect of Guangzhou, sent a letter inviting him. Han replied: "My own household is trapped as well. It is not that I do not want to come—but coming alone would accomplish nothing. We must find a way to help each other."

sentences.zh: 遂還惠州。

translations.literal: Then he returned to Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned to Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 州之惡少年正相率為盜，里落驚擾，惠人要罕出城，及郊，遮道求救護者數千計。

translations.literal: Wicked youths in the prefecture were just then banding together as robbers, villages were thrown into alarm, the people of Huizhou wanted Han to leave the city, and at the outskirts thousands blocked the road begging for protection.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked youths in the prefecture were banding together as robbers, and the countryside was in uproar. The people of Huizhou wanted Han to leave the city; at the outskirts, thousands blocked the road pleading for protection.

sentences.zh: 罕擇父老可語者問以策，曰：「吾屬皆有田客，欲給以兵，使相保聚。」

translations.literal: Han selected elders he could speak with and asked their advice. They said: "We all have tenant farmers on our lands and wish to supply them with arms so they can gather for mutual defense."
translations.idiomatic: Han chose elders he could consult and asked their advice. They said: "We all have tenant farmers on our estates. We want to arm them and have them gather for mutual defense."

sentences.zh: 罕曰：「有田客者如是，得矣，無者奈何？」

translations.literal: Han said: "For those with tenant farmers, that will do—but what of those who have none?"
translations.idiomatic: Han said: "That works for those with tenant farmers—but what about those who have none?"

sentences.zh: 乃呼耆長發里民，補壯丁，每長二百人；

translations.literal: Then he summoned the elders to muster the people of the hamlets and fill out the militia: two hundred men per elder.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned the hamlet elders to muster the local population and fill out the militia ranks—two hundred men per elder.

sentences.zh: 又令邑尉增弓手二千。

translations.literal: He also ordered the district captain to add two thousand archers.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the district captain to recruit two thousand additional archers.

sentences.zh: 巳時下令，約申而集。

translations.literal: At the si hour he issued the order, fixing assembly at the shen hour.
translations.idiomatic: At mid-morning he issued the order, setting assembly for mid-afternoon.

sentences.zh: 募有方略者，許以官秩、金帛，使為甲首。

translations.literal: He recruited men of strategic ability, promising rank and gold and silk to serve as squad leaders.
translations.idiomatic: He sought men with military skill, promising official rank and rewards of gold and silk to serve as squad leaders.

sentences.zh: 久之，無至者。

translations.literal: After a long while, none came.
translations.idiomatic: A long while passed, and no one came forward.

sentences.zh: 有婦人訴為僕奪釵珥，捕得之，並執奪攘者十八輩，皆梟首決口置道左，傳曰：「此耆長發為壯丁不肯行者也。」

translations.literal: A woman complained that a servant had robbed her of hairpins and earrings. He was caught, along with eighteen looters; all were beheaded and their mouths cut, displayed on the left of the road with the announcement: "These are militiamen called up by the elders who refused to march."
translations.idiomatic: A woman complained that a servant had stolen her hairpins and earrings. The thief was caught, along with eighteen looters. All nineteen were beheaded and their mouths slit; the heads were displayed beside the road with a proclamation: "These are militiamen summoned by the elders who refused to report for duty."

sentences.zh: 觀者始有怖色。

translations.literal: Onlookers at last showed fear.
translations.idiomatic: The onlookers at last showed fear.

sentences.zh: 至期，得六百人，尉所部亦至。

translations.literal: When the appointed time came, six hundred men had assembled, and the captain's contingent also arrived.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointed hour came, six hundred men had mustered, and the captain's force arrived as well.

sentences.zh: 於是染庫帛為旗；

translations.literal: Then he dyed cloth from the storehouse to make banners.
translations.idiomatic: He dyed cloth from the government storehouse to make banners.

sentences.zh: 授之。

translations.literal: They were distributed.
translations.idiomatic: These were handed out to the troops.

sentences.zh: 割牛革為盾形，柔之湯中，每盾削竹簽十六，穿於革，以木為鼻，使持之自蔽。

translations.literal: Cattle hides were cut into shield shapes and softened in boiling water; for each shield sixteen sharpened bamboo splints were cut, threaded through the hide, with a wooden grip, so men could hold them to shield themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He cut cattle hides into shield shapes and softened them in boiling water. Sixteen sharpened bamboo splints were threaded through each hide with a wooden grip attached, giving the men something to hold up for protection.

sentences.zh: 斷苦竹數千，銛其末，使操為兵。

translations.literal: Thousands of bitter bamboo stalks were cut and their tips sharpened for the men to wield as weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of bitter bamboo poles were cut and their tips sharpened for the men to wield as spears.

sentences.zh: 悉出公私戎器。

translations.literal: All public and private arms were brought out.
translations.idiomatic: Every public and private weapon in the city was brought out.

sentences.zh: 檄告屬城，仿而行之。

translations.literal: He sent dispatches to subordinate cities directing them to follow his example.
translations.idiomatic: He sent dispatches to the subordinate prefectures instructing them to follow his example.

sentences.zh: 數日，眾大振，向之惡少年，皆隸行伍，無敢動。

translations.literal: Within days morale surged; the former wicked youths all entered the ranks and dared not stir.
translations.idiomatic: Within days morale soared. The very youths who had been robbing now fell into the ranks and dared not stir.

sentences.zh: 乃簡卒三千，方舟建旗，伐鼓作樂，順流而下。

translations.literal: Then he selected three thousand troops, linked boats flying banners, beat drums and played music, and sailed downstream.
translations.idiomatic: He then picked three thousand troops, linked boats under banners, beat drums and played music, and sailed downstream.

sentences.zh: 將至廣，悉眾登岸，斬木為鹿角，積高數仞，營于南門。

translations.literal: As they neared Guangzhou, he landed his entire force, cut timber into cheval-de-frise barriers piled several ren high, and encamped at the South Gate.
translations.idiomatic: As they neared Guangzhou, he landed his entire force, cut timber into abatis barriers piled several ren high, and encamped at the South Gate.

sentences.zh: 智高戴黃蓋臨觀，相去三十步，見已嚴備，不敢犯。

translations.literal: Zhigao observed from beneath a yellow parasol at a distance of thirty paces; seeing the defenses ready, he did not dare attack.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao watched from beneath a yellow parasol at a distance of thirty paces. Seeing the defenses fully prepared, he did not dare attack.

sentences.zh: 罕徐開門而入，智高遂解去。

translations.literal: Han slowly opened the gates and entered; Zhigao then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Han slowly opened the gates and entered the city, and Zhigao then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時南道郵驛斷絕，罕上事，不得通；

translations.literal: At that time postal relays on the southern route were cut off, and Han's reports to the throne could not get through.
translations.idiomatic: Postal routes on the southern circuit were cut off, and Han's reports to the throne never reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 而提點刑獄鮑軻遁處南雄，數具奏。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Bao Ke, Judicial Intendant, had fled to Nanxiong and submitted several complete memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Bao Ke, the Judicial Intendant, had fled to Nanxiong and filed several detailed memorials.

sentences.zh: 及賊平，軻受賞，罕謫監信州酒。

translations.literal: When the rebels were suppressed, Ke received rewards while Han was demoted to overseer of the Xizhou wine monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion was put down, Ke received rewards while Han was demoted to overseer of the Xizhou wine monopoly.

sentences.zh: 安撫使孫沔言罕實有功，復以為西路轉運使。

translations.literal: The Pacification Commissioner Sun Mian stated that Han had truly rendered service, and he was restored as Transport Commissioner of the Western Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Sun Mian testified that Han had truly distinguished himself, and Han was restored as Transport Commissioner of the Western Circuit.

sentences.zh: 或傳智高不死，走火峒，儂宗旦據險聚眾，邕守蕭注謀擊之。

translations.literal: Some reported that Zhigao had not died but fled to Huo Tong, where Nong Zongdan held the terrain and gathered followers; Xiao Zhu, prefect of Yongzhou, planned to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread that Zhigao had survived and fled to Huo Tong, where Nong Zongdan held the high ground and gathered a following. Xiao Zhu, prefect of Yongzhou, planned an attack.

sentences.zh: 罕呼宗旦子日新謂之曰：「汝父內為交阯所仇，外為邊將希賞之餌，非計也。

translations.literal: Han summoned Zongdan's son Rixin and told him: "Your father is hated within by Jiaozhi and without is bait for frontier generals hoping for rewards—this is no good plan.
translations.idiomatic: Han summoned Zongdan's son Rixin and told him: "Your father is hated by the Vietnamese within and used as bait by frontier generals seeking rewards without. This is no viable course.

sentences.zh: 汝歸報，擇利而為之。

translations.literal: Go back and report to him—let him choose what profit lies in it and act accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Go back and tell him to weigh his options and act on whatever serves him best.

sentences.zh: 於是父子俱降。

translations.literal: Thereupon father and son both surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son then both surrendered.

sentences.zh: 徙知潭州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 擢戶部、度支副使，復為潭州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Ministry of Revenue and Fiscal Affairs, then returned to Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Ministry of Revenue and Fiscal Affairs, then returned to Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 為政務適人情，不加威罰。

translations.literal: In governing he sought to suit people's feelings and did not add harsh punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In governing he sought to accommodate human nature and did not resort to harsh punishments.

sentences.zh: 有狂婦數訴事，出言無章，卻之則勃罵，前守每叱逐之。

translations.literal: There was a madwoman who repeatedly brought lawsuits, speaking incoherently; if turned away she would fly into curses, and previous prefects always shouted and drove her off.
translations.idiomatic: A madwoman kept bringing lawsuits, her speech incoherent. Turn her away and she would burst into curses. Every previous prefect had shouted at her and driven her off.

sentences.zh: 罕獨引至前，委曲徐問，久稍可曉，乃本為人妻，無子，夫死，妾有子，遂逐婦而據家資，屢訴不得直，因憤恚發狂。

translations.literal: Han alone drew her forward and gently questioned her at length; eventually something could be understood: she had originally been a man's wife with no children; when her husband died, a concubine bore a son, drove out the wife and seized the family property; she had petitioned many times without justice and, in rage and despair, had gone mad.
translations.idiomatic: Han alone drew her forward and questioned her gently and at length. Gradually her story became clear: she had been a wife without children. When her husband died, a concubine bore a son, drove the wife out, and seized the family property. She had petitioned again and again without redress, and rage and despair had unhinged her.

sentences.zh: 罕為治妾而反其資，婦良愈，郡人傳為神明。

translations.literal: Han had the concubine punished and restored the property; the woman recovered her sanity, and the people of the prefecture spoke of him as divine.
translations.idiomatic: Han punished the concubine and restored the property to the wife. The woman recovered her sanity, and the people of the prefecture spoke of him as though he were divine.

sentences.zh: 監司上治狀，敕書褒諭，賜絹三百。

translations.literal: The supervisory commissioners reported his governance; an imperial edict praised him and granted three hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit supervisors reported his achievements in office. An imperial edict commended him and granted three hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 徙知明州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 以光祿卿卒，年八十。

translations.literal: He died as Director of the Imperial Household Provisioners at the age of eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Director of the Imperial Household Provisioners, aged eighty.

sentences.zh: 兄之子珪少孤，罕教養有恩，後珪貴，每予書，必以盛滿為戒云。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Gui was orphaned young; Han raised and nurtured him with kindness. Later, when Gui rose to eminence, Han always warned him in his letters about the dangers of reaching the full point.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother's son Wang Gui was orphaned young; Han raised him with kindness. Later, when Gui rose to high office, Han always warned him in his letters against the peril of reaching the brim.

sentences.zh: 從兄 琪

translations.literal: Paternal cousin: Qi
translations.idiomatic: Paternal cousin: Wang Qi

sentences.zh: 琪，字君玉，兒童時已能為歌詩。

translations.literal: Qi, styled Junyu, could already compose songs and poems as a child.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qi, styled Junyu, was composing songs and poems while still a child.

sentences.zh: 起進士，調江都主簿。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as chief clerk of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief clerk of Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 上時務十二事，請建義倉，置營田，減度僧，罷鬻爵，禁錦綺、珠貝，行鄉飲、籍田，復制科，興學校。

translations.literal: He submitted twelve items on affairs of the age, urging establishment of charity granaries, military colonies, reduction of ordained monks, abolition of the sale of rank, prohibition of brocade, silk gauze, pearls, and shells, revival of village drinking ceremonies and the plowing ceremony, restoration of the special examination route, and promotion of schools.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted twelve proposals on pressing affairs of state: establish charity granaries, create military colonies, reduce the number of ordained monks, abolish the sale of rank, ban brocade, silk gauze, pearls, and shells, revive the village drinking ceremony and the royal plowing rite, restore the special examination route, and promote schools.

sentences.zh: 仁宗嘉之，除館閣校勘、集賢校理。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong commended this and appointed him Collator in the Palace Library and Proofreader in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong commended the proposals and appointed him Collator in the Palace Library and Proofreader in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 帝宴太清樓，命館閣臣作《山水石歌》，琪獨蒙褒賞。

translations.literal: At a banquet in the Hall of Great Clarity, the Emperor ordered the palace scholars to compose 《Song of Mountains, Waters, and Stones》; Qi alone received special praise.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet in the Hall of Great Clarity, the emperor ordered the palace scholars to compose 《Song of Mountains, Waters, and Stones》. Qi alone won special praise.

sentences.zh: 詔通判舒州。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve as vice-prefect of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice-prefect of Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，奏發廩救民，未報，先振以公租，守以下皆不聽，琪挺身任之。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he memorialized to open the granaries to aid the people; before a reply came, he distributed relief from public rents first; the prefect and all below refused consent, but Qi stepped forward and took full responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year he memorialized to open the granaries and relieve the people. Before any reply arrived, he distributed relief from public rents on his own authority. The prefect and his subordinates all refused to go along, but Qi stepped forward and took full responsibility himself.

sentences.zh: 知復州，民毆佃客死，吏論如律。

translations.literal: As prefect of Fuzhou, a commoner beat a tenant farmer to death; the clerks argued for punishment according to law.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Fuzhou, he faced a case in which a commoner had beaten a tenant farmer to death. The clerks argued for the standard penalty under law.

sentences.zh: 琪疑之，留未決，已而新制下，凡如是者聽減死。

translations.literal: Qi had doubts and held the case undecided; soon a new statute arrived: in all such cases, reduction from death was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had doubts and kept the case open. Before long a new statute arrived: in all such cases, the death penalty could be reduced.

sentences.zh: 歷開封府推官，直集賢院、兩浙淮南轉運使、修起居注、鹽鐵判官、判戶部勾院、知制誥。

translations.literal: He served in succession as investigating officer of the Kaifeng prefecture, Director of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, Transport Commissioner of the Two Zhe and Huainan circuits, compiler of the Veritable Records, Section Chief of the Salt and Iron Commission, Section Chief of the Ministry of Revenue Audit Office, and Drafter of Proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as investigating officer of the Kaifeng prefecture, Director of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, Transport Commissioner for the Two Zhe and Huainan circuits, compiler of the Veritable Records, Section Chief of the Salt and Iron Commission, Section Chief of the Ministry of Revenue Audit Office, and Drafter of Proclamations.

sentences.zh: 嘗入對便殿，帝從容謂曰：「卿雅有心計，若三司缺使，當無以易卿。」

translations.literal: Once, entering the Privy Hall for audience, the Emperor said at ease: "You are truly shrewd in planning. If the Three Fiscal Commissions should lack a commissioner, none could replace you."
translations.idiomatic: Once, during an audience in the Privy Hall, the emperor said casually: "You have a real gift for planning. If the Three Fiscal Commissions ever need a commissioner, no one could take your place."

sentences.zh: 會奉使契丹，因感疾還，上介誣其詐，責信州團練副使。

translations.literal: Just then he was sent on mission to the Khitan and, falling ill on the way, returned; the chief envoy falsely accused him of malingering, and he was demoted to Vice Commander of the Xizhou Militia.
translations.idiomatic: Just then he was dispatched on a mission to the Khitan. He fell ill on the road and turned back. The chief envoy falsely accused him of malingering, and he was demoted to Vice Commander of the Xizhou Militia.

sentences.zh: 久之，以龍圖閣待制知潤州。

translations.literal: After a long while he was made Draftsman in Waiting at the Hall of Dragon Charts and prefect of Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was made Draftsman in Waiting at the Hall of Dragon Charts and appointed prefect of Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 轉運使欲浚常、潤漕河，琪陳其不便，詔寢役。

translations.literal: The Transport Commissioner wished to dredge the canal linking Chang and Run; Qi set forth its drawbacks, and an edict halted the project.
translations.idiomatic: The Transport Commissioner wanted to dredge the canal between Chang and Run. Qi laid out the drawbacks, and an edict halted the project.

sentences.zh: 而後議者卒請廢古城埭，破古函管而浚之，河反狹，舟不得方行，公私交病。

translations.literal: But later advocates finally persuaded the court to abandon the ancient dyke and break open the old sluice gates to dredge; the river grew narrower instead, boats could not pass side by side, and public and private interests alike suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Later advocates finally won approval to abandon the ancient dyke, break open the old sluice gates, and dredge the channel. The river grew narrower instead; boats could no longer pass side by side, and both public and private interests suffered.

sentences.zh: 徙知江寧。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 先是，府多火災，或託以鬼神，人不敢救。

translations.literal: Previously the prefecture had suffered many fires; some attributed them to spirits, and people dared not fight the flames.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the prefecture had suffered many fires. Some blamed supernatural forces, and people were afraid to fight the flames.

sentences.zh: 琪召令廂邏，具為作賞捕之法，未幾，得奸人，誅之，火患遂息。

translations.literal: Qi summoned the commandants of the wards and patrols and devised reward-and-capture regulations; before long the culprits were seized and executed, and the fires ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Qi summoned the ward and patrol commandants and devised reward-and-capture regulations. Before long the arsonists were seized and executed, and the fires stopped.

sentences.zh: 復知制誥，加樞密直學士、知鄧州，徙揚州，入判太常寺，又出知杭州，復為揚州、潤州。

translations.literal: He again served as Drafter of Proclamations, was added as Academician of the Privy Council, served as prefect of Dengzhou, was transferred to Yangzhou, entered the capital to serve as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, went out again as prefect of Hangzhou, and served again at Yangzhou and Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as Drafter of Proclamations, was made Academician of the Privy Council, served as prefect of Dengzhou, was transferred to Yangzhou, returned to the capital as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, went out again as prefect of Hangzhou, and served again at Yangzhou and Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 以禮部侍郎致仕。

translations.literal: He retired as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He retired with the rank of Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 琪性孤介，不與時合。

translations.literal: Qi was solitary and upright by nature and did not fit the temper of his times.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was solitary and upright by nature and ill suited to the temper of his age.

sentences.zh: 數臨東南名鎮，政尚簡靜。

translations.literal: He several times governed famous posts in the southeast and favored a plain, quiet style of rule.
translations.idiomatic: He governed several famous posts in the southeast and favored a plain, quiet style of administration.

sentences.zh: 每疾俗吏飾廚傳以沽名譽，故待賓客頗闊略。

translations.literal: He always despised vulgar officials who decked out their kitchens and posting stations to win reputation, and so his treatment of guests was rather sparse.
translations.idiomatic: He always despised vulgar officials who lavishly furnished their kitchens and posting stations to burnish their reputations, and so his own hospitality was notably spare.

sentences.zh: 間造飛語起謗，終不自恤。

translations.literal: From time to time slanders arose, yet he never troubled himself over them.
translations.idiomatic: Slanders arose from time to time, yet he never let them trouble him.

sentences.zh: 葬於真州。

translations.literal: He was buried at Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried at Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔真、揚二州發卒護其窆，蓋異數也。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zhen and Yang prefectures to dispatch soldiers to escort his burial—a singular honor.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Zhen and Yang prefectures to dispatch soldiers to escort his burial—a singular honor.

sentences.zh: 論曰：公亮靜重鎮浮，練達典憲，與韓琦並相，號稱老成。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Ougongliang was calm and weighty, anchoring frivolity; well versed in statutes and precedent, he served as chief minister alongside Han Qi and was hailed as a seasoned statesman.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: Zeng Gongliang was calm and weighty, a steady anchor against frivolity. Well versed in statutes and precedent, he served as chief minister alongside Han Qi and was hailed as a seasoned statesman.

sentences.zh: 升之自為言官，即著直聲。

translations.literal: Sheng Zhi, from the moment he became a remonstrating official, won renown for blunt integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Sheng Zhi, from the moment he became a remonstrating official, won renown for blunt integrity.

sentences.zh: 然皆挾術任數，公亮疾琦專任，薦王安石以間之，升之陰助安石，陽為異同，以避清議，二人措慮如此，豈誠心謀國者乎？

translations.literal: Yet all relied on stratagem and schemes. Ougongliang resented Qi's monopolization of power and recommended Wang Anshi to drive a wedge between them. Sheng Zhi secretly aided Anshi while outwardly feigning disagreement to evade the censure of upright opinion. With such calculations by the two of them, could they truly have been men who whole-heartedly sought the good of the state?
translations.idiomatic: Yet both relied on stratagem and scheming. Zeng Gongliang resented Han Qi's monopoly on power and recommended Wang Anshi to drive a wedge between them. Chen Sheng Zhi secretly aided Wang Anshi while outwardly feigning disagreement to dodge the censure of upright opinion. By calculations such as these, could either man truly have been one who whole-heartedly sought the good of the state?

sentences.zh: 新法之行，何望其能正救也。

translations.literal: With the New Policies in force, how could one hope they could set things right and save the realm?
translations.idiomatic: With the New Policies in force, how could one hope they could set things right and save the realm?

sentences.zh: 及安石去位，充、珪實代之，天下喁喁，思有所休息。

translations.literal: When Anshi left office, Chong and Gui in fact replaced him; throughout the realm people murmured, longing for some respite.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anshi left office, Wu Chong and Wang Gui in fact replaced him. Throughout the realm people murmured, longing for some respite.

sentences.zh: 充力不逮心，同僚左掣右伺，至鞅鞅以死，傷哉，其不足與有行也。

translations.literal: Chong's strength did not match his intent; colleagues pulled from the left and watched from the right, until he died discontented. How sad—he was not equal to accomplishing the task.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chong's strength did not match his intent. Colleagues pulled from the left and watched from the right, until he died discontented. How sad—he was not equal to accomplishing the task.

sentences.zh: 珪容身固位，于勢何所重輕，而陰忌正人，以濟其患失之謀，鄙夫可與事君也與哉！

translations.literal: Gui preserved himself and secured his post—what weight did he add or subtract to the balance of power? Yet he secretly resented upright men to advance his scheme of fearing loss, and one may ask: can a base fellow be entrusted with serving his sovereign?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui preserved himself and secured his post—what weight did he add or subtract to the balance of power? Yet he secretly resented upright men to advance his scheme of fearing loss. One may ask: can a base fellow be entrusted with serving his sovereign?
